<body>
  <div class="brief">
    <h1>Working tabs wireframe</h1>
    <p>Click only selects. The tab stack docks the whole pane. A tab’s own menu sends that tab into a pool or another group. Ctrl-click several tabs, then right-click, to send them together. Right-click a sidebar row for the same send commands.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="stage">
    <div class="window">
      <aside>
        <input class="search" value="" placeholder="Search tabs and groups…" disabled />
        <div class="tree" id="tree"></div>
      </aside>
      <main>
        <div class="workspace" id="workspace"></div>
      </main>
      <div class="status" id="status">Click a tab to select it. The pane stays where it is.</div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div id="menu" class="menu hidden"></div>
<script>
const sections = [
  { id: "nav", title: "Navigation", color: "#d45d97" },
  { id: "work", title: "Work", color: "#e08b3c" },
];

let groups = [
  { id: "sast", title: "SAST", sectionId: "nav", color: "#d45d97" },
  { id: "main", title: "Main", sectionId: "nav", color: "#8b6fd6" },
  { id: "home", title: "Home", sectionId: "nav", color: "#43a047" },
  { id: "qisl", title: "QISL Platform", sectionId: "work", color: "#e08b3c", dock: "main" },
  { id: "harness", title: "Tool Harness", sectionId: "work", color: "#2fa3a3" },
  { id: "sfa", title: "SFA", sectionId: "work", color: "#4a7fe0" },
  { id: "pay", title: "Payment Gateway", sectionId: "work", color: "#d0a215" },
  { id: "ext", title: "External Services", sectionId: "work", color: "#d1453b" },
];

let tabs = [
  { id: "a", title: "Architecture and Design of a Decoupled…", groupId: "qisl", order: 0 },
  { id: "b", title: "Session Recovery — Backend Gr…", groupId: "qisl", order: 1 },
  { id: "c", title: "Belial Dreams", groupId: "qisl", order: 2 },
  { id: "d", title: "Terminus 1", groupId: "qisl", order: 3 },
  { id: "e", title: "QISL Platform", groupId: "qisl", order: 4 },
  { id: "f", title: "Payment notes", groupId: "ext", order: 0 },
  { id: "g", title: "Theme registry", groupId: "harness", order: 0 },
];

let activeId = "e";
let selected = new Set(["e"]);
let sideSelected = null;
let seq = 1;

const tree = document.getElementById("tree");
const workspace = document.getElementById("workspace");
const status = document.getElementById("status");
const menu = document.getElementById("menu");

function groupById(id) { return groups.find((g) => g.id === id); }
function sectionById(id) { return sections.find((s) => s.id === id); }
function tabById(id) { return tabs.find((t) => t.id === id); }

function say(text) { status.textContent = text; }

function tabsInGroup(groupId) {
  return tabs
    .filter((t) => t.groupId === groupId && !t.poolSectionId)
    .sort((a, b) => a.order - b.order);
}

/** Open leaves stay in the pane even after the sidebar row is filed in a pool. */
function tabsOnPane(groupId) {
  return tabs.filter((t) => t.groupId === groupId).sort((a, b) => a.order - b.order);
}

function poolTabs(sectionId) {
  return tabs.filter((t) => t.poolSectionId === sectionId);
}

function visibleGroups() {
  return groups.filter((g) => g.dock);
}

function render() {
  renderTree();
  renderWorkspace();
}

function renderTree() {
  tree.replaceChildren();
  for (const section of sections) {
    const label = el("div", "sec-label");
    label.append(el("span", "chev", "›"), document.createTextNode(section.title));
    const owned = groups.filter((g) => g.sectionId === section.id).length;
    label.append(el("span", "count", String(owned)));
    tree.append(label);

    const tray = el("div", "pool");
    tray.dataset.sectionId = section.id;
    tray.addEventListener("dragover", (evt) => evt.preventDefault());
    tray.addEventListener("drop", (evt) => {
      evt.preventDefault();
      const ids = takeDrag(evt);
      if (ids.length) sendToPool(ids, section.id);
    });
    tray.append(el("div", "cap", section.title + " pool"));
    const parked = poolTabs(section.id);
    if (parked.length === 0) tray.append(el("div", "empty", "Drop or send tabs here. They stay open."));
    for (const tab of parked) {
      const home = groupById(tab.origin?.groupId ?? tab.groupId);
      const row = tabRow(tab, home ? "returns to " + home.title : "");
      tray.append(row);
    }
    tree.append(tray);

    for (const group of groups.filter((g) => g.sectionId === section.id)) {
      const kids = tabsInGroup(group.id);
      const row = el("div", "row" + (sideSelected === group.id ? " selected" : ""));
      const bar = el("span", "bar");
      bar.style.background = group.color;
      row.append(bar, el("span", "chev", "›"), el("span", "name", group.title));
      const meta = group.dock ? "on screen" : "not on screen";
      row.append(el("span", "meta", kids.length + " · " + meta));
      row.addEventListener("click", () => {
        sideSelected = group.id;
        say("Selected the " + group.title + " group. The pane stayed where it is.");
        render();
      });
      row.addEventListener("contextmenu", (evt) => openMenu(evt, groupMenu(group)));
      row.addEventListener("dragover", (evt) => evt.preventDefault());
      row.addEventListener("drop", (evt) => {
        evt.preventDefault();
        evt.stopPropagation();
        const ids = takeDrag(evt);
        if (ids.length) sendToGroup(ids, group.id);
      });
      tree.append(row);
      for (const tab of kids) tree.append(tabRow(tab, ""));
    }
  }
}

function tabRow(tab, hint) {
  const row = el("div", "row" + (sideSelected === tab.id ? " selected" : ""));
  row.style.paddingLeft = "28px";
  const name = el("span", "name");
  name.textContent = tab.title;
  if (hint) name.append(el("span", "home-hint", hint));
  row.append(el("span", "chev", "·"), name);
  if (tab.poolSectionId) row.append(el("span", "mark", "pool"));
  row.addEventListener("click", () => {
    sideSelected = tab.id;
    say("Selected “" + tab.title + "”. Nothing opened and nothing moved.");
    render();
  });
  row.addEventListener("contextmenu", (evt) => {
    sideSelected = tab.id;
    openMenu(evt, tabMenu([tab.id], "sidebar"));
    render();
  });
  row.draggable = true;
  row.addEventListener("dragstart", (evt) => setDrag(evt, tab.id));
  return row;
}

function renderWorkspace() {
  workspace.replaceChildren();
  for (const edge of ["top", "left", "main", "right", "bottom"]) {
    const cell = el("div", "cell");
    cell.dataset.edge = edge;
    for (const group of visibleGroups().filter((g) => (g.dock || "main") === edge)) {
      cell.append(frameFor(group));
    }
    workspace.append(cell);
  }
}

function frameFor(group) {
  const frame = el("div", "frame" + (group.dock && group.dock !== "main" ? " docked" : ""));
  const bar = el("div", "tabbar");
  const strip = el("div", "tabs");
  for (const tab of tabsOnPane(group.id)) {
    const chip = el("div", "chip" + (tab.id === activeId ? " active" : "") + (selected.has(tab.id) ? " picked" : ""));
    const label = el("span", "label", tab.title);
    chip.append(label);
    if (tab.poolSectionId) chip.append(el("span", "mark", "pool"));
    chip.draggable = true;
    chip.addEventListener("dragstart", (evt) => setDrag(evt, tab.id));
    chip.addEventListener("click", (evt) => {
      if (evt.ctrlKey || evt.metaKey) {
        if (selected.has(tab.id)) selected.delete(tab.id);
        else selected.add(tab.id);
        say(selected.size + " tabs selected. Right-click to send them. The pane stayed put.");
      } else {
        selected = new Set([tab.id]);
        activeId = tab.id;
        say("Showing “" + tab.title + "” in the pane already on screen.");
      }
      render();
    });
    chip.addEventListener("contextmenu", (evt) => {
      const ids = selected.has(tab.id) && selected.size > 1 ? [...selected] : [tab.id];
      if (ids.length === 1) {
        selected = new Set([tab.id]);
        activeId = tab.id;
      }
      openMenu(evt, tabMenu(ids, "tab"));
      render();
    });
    strip.append(chip);
  }
  const stack = el("div", "stack-btn", "▾");
  stack.title = "Tab stack";
  stack.addEventListener("click", (evt) => openMenu(evt, stackMenu(group)));
  stack.addEventListener("contextmenu", (evt) => openMenu(evt, stackMenu(group)));
  bar.append(strip, stack);
  const doc = el("div", "doc");
  const shown = tabById(activeId);
  const inThis = shown && shown.groupId === group.id;
  doc.append(el("h2", "", inThis ? shown.title : group.title));
  doc.append(el("p", "", inThis
    ? (shown.poolSectionId
      ? "Still open in this pane. The sidebar row sits in the " + sectionById(shown.poolSectionId).title + " pool."
      : "This note is already in this pane. Selecting it here does not create a split.")
    : "This pane belongs to " + group.title + "."));
  frame.append(bar, doc);
  return frame;
}

function groupMenu(group) {
  return {
    title: group.title,
    items: [
      { label: "Dock group", hint: "whole pane", children: dockItems((edge) => dockGroup(group.id, edge)) },
      { sep: true },
      { label: "Obsidian: Close all", dim: true, run: () => say("Left as Obsidian’s own Close all.") },
    ],
  };
}

function stackMenu(group) {
  const items = tabsOnPane(group.id).map((tab) => ({
    label: tab.title,
    run: () => {
      selected = new Set([tab.id]);
      activeId = tab.id;
      say("Picked “" + tab.title + "” from the stack. The pane stayed put.");
      render();
    },
  }));
  items.push({ sep: true });
  items.push({ label: "Dock group", hint: "whole pane", children: dockItems((edge) => dockGroup(group.id, edge)) });
  items.push({
    label: "Send every tab to pool",
    hint: "leaves stay",
      children: sections.map((section) => ({
      label: section.title,
      run: () => sendToPool(tabsOnPane(group.id).map((t) => t.id), section.id),
    })),
  });
  return { title: "Stack · " + group.title, hint: "Dock moves every tab in this pane together.", items };
}

function tabMenu(ids, source) {
  const many = ids.length > 1;
  const first = tabById(ids[0]);
  const items = [];
  if (source === "tab") {
    items.push({ label: many ? "Obsidian: Close selected" : "Obsidian: Close", dim: true, run: () => say("Left as Obsidian’s own command.") });
    items.push({ label: many ? "Obsidian: Pin selected" : "Obsidian: Pin", dim: true, run: () => say("Left as Obsidian’s own command.") });
    items.push({ sep: true });
  }
  items.push({
    label: many ? "Send " + ids.length + " tabs to pool" : "Send to pool",
    hint: "leaf stays",
    children: sections.map((section) => ({
      label: section.title,
      run: () => sendToPool(ids, section.id),
    })),
  });
  items.push({
    label: many ? "Send " + ids.length + " tabs to group" : "Send to group",
    hint: "no reveal",
    children: groups.filter((g) => !g.peeled).map((group) => ({
      label: group.title,
      dim: ids.every((id) => tabById(id).groupId === group.id && !tabById(id).poolSectionId),
      run: () => sendToGroup(ids, group.id),
    })),
  });
  const returnable = ids.filter((id) => tabById(id).origin);
  if (returnable.length) {
    items.push({
      label: returnable.length > 1 ? "Return each to its own group" : "Return to " + (groupById(tabById(returnable[0]).origin.groupId)?.title ?? "origin"),
      run: () => restore(returnable),
    });
  }
  items.push({ sep: true });
  items.push({
    label: many ? "Dock selected together" : "Dock this tab",
    hint: "one pane",
    children: dockItems((edge) => peel(ids, edge)),
  });
  return { title: many ? ids.length + " tabs" : first.title, hint: source === "sidebar" ? "Same commands as the tab header." : "", items };
}

function dockItems(run) {
  return [
    ["Dock left", "left"],
    ["Dock right", "right"],
    ["Dock top", "top"],
    ["Dock bottom", "bottom"],
  ].map(([label, edge]) => ({ label, run: () => run(edge) }));
}

function sendToPool(ids, sectionId) {
  const section = sectionById(sectionId);
  for (const id of ids) {
    const tab = tabById(id);
    if (!tab.origin) tab.origin = { groupId: tab.groupId, order: tab.order };
    tab.poolSectionId = sectionId;
  }
  selected = new Set(ids);
  say("Filed " + ids.length + " tab" + (ids.length > 1 ? "s" : "") + " in the " + section.title + " pool. " + (ids.length > 1 ? "They remember" : "It remembers") + " where " + (ids.length > 1 ? "they" : "it") + " came from. No pane moved.");
  closeMenu();
  render();
}

function sendToGroup(ids, groupId) {
  const group = groupById(groupId);
  let order = tabsInGroup(groupId).reduce((max, tab) => Math.max(max, tab.order), -1);
  for (const id of ids) {
    const tab = tabById(id);
    if (tab.groupId === groupId && !tab.poolSectionId) continue;
    tab.poolSectionId = null;
    tab.origin = null;
    tab.groupId = groupId;
    tab.order = ++order;
  }
  say("Sent " + ids.length + " tab" + (ids.length > 1 ? "s" : "") + " to " + group.title + ". " + (group.dock ? "That pane is on screen." : "That pane stayed off screen, and this view did not jump to it.") + " This is their new home.");
  closeMenu();
  render();
}

function restore(ids) {
  for (const id of ids) {
    const tab = tabById(id);
    if (!tab.origin) continue;
    tab.groupId = tab.origin.groupId;
    tab.order = tab.origin.order;
    tab.poolSectionId = null;
    tab.origin = null;
  }
  say("Put back in the group " + (ids.length > 1 ? "each tab" : "it") + " left. The view did not jump.");
  closeMenu();
  render();
}

function dockGroup(groupId, edge) {
  const group = groupById(groupId);
  group.dock = edge;
  say("Docked the " + group.title + " pane to the " + edge + ". Every tab in that pane moved together.");
  closeMenu();
  render();
}

function peel(ids, edge) {
  const id = "peel" + seq++;
  const title = ids.length === 1 ? tabById(ids[0]).title : ids.length + " tabs";
  groups.push({ id, title, sectionId: "work", color: "#7eb6d6", dock: edge, peeled: true });
  let order = 0;
  for (const tabId of ids) {
    const tab = tabById(tabId);
    tab.poolSectionId = null;
    tab.origin = null;
    tab.groupId = id;
    tab.order = order++;
  }
  say("Peeled " + ids.length + " tab" + (ids.length > 1 ? "s" : "") + " into " + (ids.length > 1 ? "their" : "its") + " own pane on the " + edge + ". The rest of the group stayed.");
  closeMenu();
  render();
}

function openMenu(evt, spec) {
  evt.preventDefault();
  evt.stopPropagation();
  menu.replaceChildren();
  if (spec.hint) menu.append(el("div", "hint", spec.hint));
  for (const item of spec.items) {
    if (item.sep) {
      menu.append(el("div", "sep"));
      continue;
    }
    const row = el("div", "mi" + (item.dim ? " dim" : ""));
    row.append(document.createTextNode(item.label));
    if (item.hint) row.append(el("span", "k", item.hint));
    if (item.children) {
      row.append(el("span", "k", "›"));
      const sub = el("div", "sub");
      for (const child of item.children) {
        const subRow = el("div", "mi" + (child.dim ? " dim" : ""), child.label);
        subRow.addEventListener("click", (e) => {
          e.stopPropagation();
          if (!child.dim) child.run();
        });
        sub.append(subRow);
      }
      row.append(sub);
      row.addEventListener("mouseenter", () => row.classList.add("open"));
      row.addEventListener("mouseleave", () => row.classList.remove("open"));
    } else {
      row.addEventListener("click", (e) => {
        e.stopPropagation();
        item.run();
      });
    }
    menu.append(row);
  }
  menu.classList.remove("hidden");
  const pad = 8;
  const rect = menu.getBoundingClientRect();
  let x = evt.clientX;
  let y = evt.clientY;
  if (x + rect.width > window.innerWidth - pad) x = window.innerWidth - rect.width - pad;
  if (y + rect.height > window.innerHeight - pad) y = window.innerHeight - rect.height - pad;
  menu.style.left = x + "px";
  menu.style.top = y + "px";
}

function closeMenu() { menu.classList.add("hidden"); }

function setDrag(evt, id) {
  const ids = selected.has(id) && selected.size > 1 ? [...selected] : [id];
  evt.dataTransfer.setData("text/plain", ids.join(","));
  evt.dataTransfer.effectAllowed = "move";
}

function takeDrag(evt) {
  return (evt.dataTransfer.getData("text/plain") || "").split(",").filter((id) => tabById(id));
}

function el(tag, className, text) {
  const node = document.createElement(tag);
  if (className) node.className = className;
  if (text != null) node.textContent = text;
  return node;
}

document.addEventListener("click", (evt) => {
  if (!menu.contains(evt.target)) closeMenu();
});
document.addEventListener("keydown", (evt) => {
  if (evt.key === "Escape") closeMenu();
});

render();
</script>
</body>
</html>

```

Three rules are in that page, taken from the screenshots and from what the plugin already does.

**A pool is a tray on the section.** Sending Belial Dreams to the Work pool left it open in the QISL Platform pane, marked `pool`, and listed it in the tray as “returns to QISL Platform”. Return put the row back under that group. The view did not jump.

**The tab stack docks the group.** Dock left moved every tab in the QISL Platform pane together. The same four edges already exist as `dockGroup` on the sidebar group menu. They are not on the stack dropdown you opened in the second screenshot.

**A named group is a new home.** Sending two selected tabs to Tool Harness took them out of this pane and did not reveal Tool Harness. That matches the multiselect menu in your fourth screenshot. Return is only for a tab sitting in a pool. A send to a group you named does not keep the old home.

One module should own that, with two operations: `send(tabs, destination)` and `dock(group, edge)`. Destination is a pool, a group, or the remembered origin. The sidebar menu, the native tab menu, the stack dropdown, and the multiselect menu are four adapters over that same pair. Today the sidebar tab menu already has “Dock this tab” and “Move to” a live group, and a row click calls `focusTab`, which is what flings panes around. The native menus in your screenshots do not call those commands yet.

The multiselect menu in the fourth screenshot is Obsidian’s own (Close selected, Pin selected, Move selected to new window). Sending the selection is the same `send`. Hooking that particular menu is the one adapter that is less certain than the single-tab menu.

	try {

	} catch (error) {
		const detail = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
		const windowsHint = process.platform === "win32"
			? " On Windows, use forward slashes or double every backslash in paths."

	const manifestPath = join(projectRoot, "manifest.json");
	const manifest = readStrictJson(manifestPath, "Plugin manifest");
	if (!manifest || typeof manifest !== "object" || Array.isArray(manifest)) {
		throw new Error("Plugin manifest must be a JSON object.");
	}
	if (typeof manifest.id !== "string" || !/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/.test(manifest.id)) {
		throw new Error("Plugin manifest has an invalid id.");
	}

}

function strictConfig(value) {
	if (!value || typeof value !== "object" || Array.isArray(value)) {
		throw new Error("Deployment config must be a JSON object.");
	}

	const allowed = new Set(["$schema", "vaults", "backup"]);
	for (const key of Object.keys(value)) {
		if (!allowed.has(key)) throw new Error(`Unknown config property: ${key}`);
	}
	if (value.$schema !== undefined && typeof value.$schema !== "string") {
		throw new Error('Config property "$schema" must be a string.');

				throw new Error("Each vault must be an object.");
			}

			for (const key of Object.keys(entry)) {
				if (!allowed.has(key)) throw new Error(`Unknown vault property: ${key}`);
			}
			if (typeof entry.name !== "string" || !entry.name.trim()) {
				throw new Error("Each vault requires a non-empty name.");
			}
			if (typeof entry.path !== "string" || !entry.path.trim()) {
				throw new Error("Each vault requires a non-empty path.");
			}
			if (typeof entry.enabled !== "boolean") {
				throw new Error("Each vault requires an enabled boolean.");
			}

			const name = expandEnvironment(entry.name, environment);
			const path = expandEnvironment(entry.path, environment);
			if (!name.trim() || !path.trim()) {

}

	} else if (existsSync(bundledNpmCli)) {
		argumentsList = [bundledNpmCli, "run", "build"];
	} else if (process.platform !== "win32") {
		executable = "npm";
		argumentsList = ["run", "build"];
	} else {
		throw new Error("Could not resolve the npm CLI without a shell command.");
	}

	const result = spawnSync(executable, argumentsList, {
		cwd: projectRoot,
		stdio: "inherit",
		shell: false,
	});

			? resolve(vault.path)
			: resolve(projectRoot, vault.path);

			throw new Error(`Vault does not exist: ${vaultRoot}`);
		}

		const configDirectory = join(vaultRoot, ".obsidian");
		assertNoSymlinks(configDirectory);
		if (!existsSync(configDirectory) || !statSync(configDirectory).isDirectory()) {

		if (overlapsProject) {

		}

		return { ...vault, vaultRoot, pluginRoot, files: [] };
	});

	for (let left = 0; left < destinations.length; left++) {
		for (let right = left + 1; right < destinations.length; right++) {
			const overlaps = isInsideOrEqual(
				destinations[left].pluginRoot,
				destinations[right].pluginRoot,
			) || isInsideOrEqual(
				destinations[right].pluginRoot,
				destinations[left].pluginRoot,

			if (overlaps) {

				throw new Error(`Missing release file: ${source}`);
			}
			assertNoSymlinks(source);

			assertNoSymlinks(target);

			const targetExists = existsSync(target);
			if (targetExists && !statSync(target).isFile()) {

			}

				source,

	if (existsSync(path)) unlinkSync(path);
}

function commitPlan(plan, { backup, deploymentId, dryRun, hooks = {} }) {
	const summary = plan.map((vault) => ({
		name: vault.name,
		path: vault.vaultRoot,
		pluginPath: vault.pluginRoot,
		changed: vault.files.filter((file) => file.changed).map((file) => file.name),
		unchanged: vault.files.filter((file) => !file.changed).map((file) => file.name),
		backupPath: null,
	}));

	if (dryRun) {
		return {
			dryRun: true,
			changed: summary.some((vault) => vault.changed.length > 0),
			vaults: summary,
		};
	}

	let committedFileCount = 0;

		for (const vault of plan) {
			mkdirSync(vault.pluginRoot, { recursive: true });
			assertNoSymlinks(vault.pluginRoot);
			const changed = vault.files.filter((file) => file.changed);
			if (changed.length === 0) continue;

			const durableBackup = backup
				? join(vault.pluginRoot, ".working-tabs-backups", deploymentId)
				: null;
			const rollbackRoot = join(
				vault.pluginRoot,
				`.working-tabs-rollback-${deploymentId}`,
			);
			const summaryEntry = summary.find(
				(entry) => entry.pluginPath === vault.pluginRoot,
			);

			if (durableBackup) {
				mkdirSync(durableBackup, { recursive: true });
				summaryEntry.backupPath = durableBackup;
			}
			mkdirSync(rollbackRoot, { recursive: true });

			for (const file of changed) {
				if (hooks.beforeCommit) {
					hooks.beforeCommit({
						vault,
						file,
						index: committedFileCount,
						deploymentId,
					});
				}

				const stage = join(
					vault.pluginRoot,
					`.${file.name}.working-tabs-stage-${deploymentId}`,
				);
				copyFileSync(file.source, stage);
				let rollbackPath = join(rollbackRoot, file.name);
				if (existsSync(file.target)) {
					if (durableBackup) {
						copyFileSync(file.target, join(durableBackup, file.name));
					}
					renameSync(file.target, rollbackPath);
				} else {
					rollbackPath = null;
				}

				committed.push({ file, stage, rollbackPath, rollbackRoot });
				try {
					renameSync(stage, file.target);
					committedFileCount++;
				} catch (error) {
					removeFileIfPresent(stage);
					throw error;
				}
			}
		}
	} catch (error) {
		const failures = [];
		for (const entry of committed.reverse()) {
			try {
				removeFileIfPresent(entry.file.target);
				if (entry.rollbackPath && existsSync(entry.rollbackPath)) {
					renameSync(entry.rollbackPath, entry.file.target);
				}
				removeFileIfPresent(entry.stage);
			} catch (rollbackError) {
				failures.push(
					`${entry.file.target}: ${
						rollbackError instanceof Error
							? rollbackError.message
							: String(rollbackError)
					}`,
				);
			}
		}

		for (const vault of plan) {
			const rollbackRoot = join(
				vault.pluginRoot,
				`.working-tabs-rollback-${deploymentId}`,
			);
			if (existsSync(rollbackRoot)) {
				try {
					rmdirSync(rollbackRoot);
				} catch (cleanupError) {
					failures.push(
						`${rollbackRoot}: ${
							cleanupError instanceof Error
								? cleanupError.message
								: String(cleanupError)
						}`,
					);
				}
			}
		}

		const suffix = failures.length
			? ` Rollback also failed for: ${failures.join("; ")}`
			: " All completed writes were rolled back.";
		throw new Error(
			`${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}${suffix}`,
		);
	}

	for (const entry of committed) {
		removeFileIfPresent(entry.stage);
		if (entry.rollbackPath) removeFileIfPresent(entry.rollbackPath);
	}
	for (const vault of plan) {
		const rollbackRoot = join(
			vault.pluginRoot,
			`.working-tabs-rollback-${deploymentId}`,
		);
		if (existsSync(rollbackRoot)) rmdirSync(rollbackRoot);
	}

	return {
		dryRun: false,
		changed: summary.some((vault) => vault.changed.length > 0),
		vaults: summary,
	};
}

export function deployRelease(options = {}) {
	const projectRoot = resolve(options.projectRoot ?? PROJECT_ROOT);
	assertNoSymlinks(projectRoot);
	const config = options.configPath ? readConfig(options.configPath, projectRoot) : null;
	const environment = options.environment ?? process.env;
	const vaults = parseVaults(config, options.vaults ?? [], environment);
	const backup = config?.backup ?? options.backup ?? true;
	if (typeof backup !== "boolean") throw new Error("Backup option must be boolean.");

	const manifest = readManifest(projectRoot);
	const destinations = preflightDestinations(vaults, manifest.id, projectRoot);
	if (!options.skipBuild) buildRelease(projectRoot);
	const plan = createPlan(destinations, projectRoot);
	const deploymentId = options.deploymentId ?? `deploy-${Date.now()}-${process.pid}`;
	if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$/.test(deploymentId)) {
		throw new Error("Deployment identifier is not safe.");
	}

	return commitPlan(plan, {
		backup,
		deploymentId,
		dryRun: Boolean(options.dryRun),
		hooks: options.hooks,
	});
}

export function parseArguments(argumentsList) {
	const options = {
		configPath: null,
		vaults: [],
		dryRun: false,
		skipBuild: false,
	};

	for (let index = 0; index < argumentsList.length; index++) {
		const argument = argumentsList[index];
		if (argument === "--dry-run") options.dryRun = true;
		else if (argument === "--skip-build") options.skipBuild = true;
		else if (argument === "--config") {
			const value = argumentsList[++index];
			if (!value) throw new Error("--config requires a path.");
			options.configPath = value;
		} else if (argument === "--vault") {
			const value = argumentsList[++index];
			if (!value) throw new Error("--vault requires a path.");
			options.vaults.push(value);
		} else if (argument === "--help" || argument === "-h") options.help = true;
		else throw new Error(`Unknown argument: ${argument}`);
	}

	return options;
}

const LOCAL_CONFIG_NAME = "working-tabs-deploy.local.json";

function usage() {
	console.log(
		"Usage: node scripts/deploy.mjs [--config path] [--vault path ...] [--dry-run] [--skip-build]",
	);
	console.log(
		`With no --config and no --vault, ${LOCAL_CONFIG_NAME} is used when it exists.`,
	);
}

if (
	process.argv[1]
	&& resolve(process.argv[1]) === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)
) {
	try {
		const options = parseArguments(process.argv.slice(2));
		if (options.help) usage();
		else console.log(JSON.stringify(deployRelease(options), null, 2));
	} catch (error) {
		console.error(error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error));
		process.exitCode = 1;
	}
}

	const absolute = resolve(candidate);
	const root = parse(absolute).root;
	let current = root;

	for (const component of relative(root, absolute).split(sep).filter(Boolean)) {
		current = join(current, component);
		if (!existsSync(current)) continue;
		if (lstatSync(current).isSymbolicLink()) {
			throw new Error(`Symbolic links are not allowed in deployment paths: ${current}`);
		}
	}
}

function expandEnvironment(value, environment) {
	return value.replace(/\$\{([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\}/g, (_match, name) => {
		const replacement = environment[name];
		if (replacement === undefined) {
			throw new Error(
				`Environment variable ${name} is required by the deployment configuration.`,
			);
		}
		return replacement;
	});
}

function readStrictJson(path, description) {
	assertNoSymlinks(path);
	if (!existsSync(path) || !statSync(path).isFile()) {
		throw new Error(`${description} does not exist: ${path}`);
	}

	try {
		return JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, "utf8"));
	} catch (error) {
		const detail = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
		const windowsHint = process.platform === "win32"
			? " On Windows, use forward slashes or double every backslash in paths."
			: "";
		throw new Error(`${description} is not strict JSON: ${path} (${detail}).${windowsHint}`);
	}
}

function readManifest(projectRoot) {
	const manifestPath = join(projectRoot, "manifest.json");
	const manifest = readStrictJson(manifestPath, "Plugin manifest");
	if (!manifest || typeof manifest !== "object" || Array.isArray(manifest)) {
		throw new Error("Plugin manifest must be a JSON object.");
	}
	if (typeof manifest.id !== "string" || !/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/.test(manifest.id)) {
		throw new Error("Plugin manifest has an invalid id.");
	}
	return manifest;
}

function strictConfig(value) {
	if (!value || typeof value !== "object" || Array.isArray(value)) {
		throw new Error("Deployment config must be a JSON object.");
	}

	const allowed = new Set(["$schema", "vaults", "backup"]);
	for (const key of Object.keys(value)) {
		if (!allowed.has(key)) throw new Error(`Unknown config property: ${key}`);
	}
	if (value.$schema !== undefined && typeof value.$schema !== "string") {
		throw new Error('Config property "$schema" must be a string.');
	}
	if (typeof value.backup !== "boolean") {
		throw new Error('Config property "backup" must be boolean.');
	}
	if (!Array.isArray(value.vaults) || value.vaults.length === 0) {
		throw new Error('Config property "vaults" must be a non-empty array.');
	}
	return value;
}

function parseVaults(config, vaultArgs, environment) {
	const configured = config
		? strictConfig(config).vaults.map((entry) => {
			if (!entry || typeof entry !== "object" || Array.isArray(entry)) {
				throw new Error("Each vault must be an object.");
			}

			const allowed = new Set(["name", "path", "enabled"]);
			for (const key of Object.keys(entry)) {
				if (!allowed.has(key)) throw new Error(`Unknown vault property: ${key}`);
			}
			if (typeof entry.name !== "string" || !entry.name.trim()) {
				throw new Error("Each vault requires a non-empty name.");
			}
			if (typeof entry.path !== "string" || !entry.path.trim()) {
				throw new Error("Each vault requires a non-empty path.");
			}
			if (typeof entry.enabled !== "boolean") {
				throw new Error("Each vault requires an enabled boolean.");
			}

			const name = expandEnvironment(entry.name, environment);
			const path = expandEnvironment(entry.path, environment);
			if (!name.trim() || !path.trim()) {
				throw new Error("Expanded vault names and paths must be non-empty.");
			}
			return { name, path, enabled: entry.enabled };
		})
		: [];

	const overrides = vaultArgs.map((vaultPath, index) => ({
		name: `Command-line vault ${index + 1}`,
		path: expandEnvironment(vaultPath, environment),
		enabled: true,
	}));

	return configured.concat(overrides).filter((vault) => vault.enabled);
}

function readConfig(configPath, projectRoot) {
	if (!configPath) return null;
	const absolute = isAbsolute(configPath)
		? resolve(configPath)
		: resolve(projectRoot, configPath);
	return readStrictJson(absolute, "Deployment config");
}

function sha256(path) {
	return createHash("sha256").update(readFileSync(path)).digest("hex");
}

function buildRelease(projectRoot) {
	const bundledNpmCli = join(
		dirname(process.execPath),
		"node_modules",
		"npm",
		"bin",
		"npm-cli.js",
	);
	const npmExecPath = process.env.npm_execpath;
	let executable = process.execPath;
	let argumentsList;

	if (npmExecPath && existsSync(npmExecPath) && /\.(?:c?js)$/.test(npmExecPath)) {
		argumentsList = [npmExecPath, "run", "build"];
	} else if (existsSync(bundledNpmCli)) {
		argumentsList = [bundledNpmCli, "run", "build"];
	} else if (process.platform !== "win32") {
		executable = "npm";
		argumentsList = ["run", "build"];
	} else {
		throw new Error("Could not resolve the npm CLI without a shell command.");
	}

	const result = spawnSync(executable, argumentsList, {
		cwd: projectRoot,
		stdio: "inherit",
		shell: false,
	});
	if (result.error) throw new Error(`Build failed: ${result.error.message}`);
	if (result.status !== 0) {
		throw new Error(`Build failed with exit code ${result.status ?? "unknown"}.`);
	}
}

function preflightDestinations(vaults, pluginId, projectRoot) {
	if (vaults.length === 0) throw new Error("No enabled vaults were configured.");

	const destinations = vaults.map((vault) => {
		const vaultRoot = isAbsolute(vault.path)
			? resolve(vault.path)
			: resolve(projectRoot, vault.path);
		assertNoSymlinks(vaultRoot);
		if (!existsSync(vaultRoot) || !statSync(vaultRoot).isDirectory()) {
			throw new Error(`Vault does not exist: ${vaultRoot}`);
		}

		const configDirectory = join(vaultRoot, ".obsidian");
		assertNoSymlinks(configDirectory);
		if (!existsSync(configDirectory) || !statSync(configDirectory).isDirectory()) {
			throw new Error(
				`Path is not an Obsidian vault because .obsidian is missing: ${vaultRoot}`,
			);
		}
		accessSync(configDirectory, constants.R_OK | constants.W_OK);

		const pluginRoot = join(configDirectory, "plugins", pluginId);
		assertNoSymlinks(pluginRoot);
		const overlapsProject = isInsideOrEqual(projectRoot, pluginRoot)
			|| isInsideOrEqual(pluginRoot, projectRoot);
		if (overlapsProject) {
			throw new Error(`Unsafe deployment destination overlaps the project source: ${pluginRoot}`);
		}

		return { ...vault, vaultRoot, pluginRoot, files: [] };
	});

	for (let left = 0; left < destinations.length; left++) {
		for (let right = left + 1; right < destinations.length; right++) {
			const overlaps = isInsideOrEqual(
				destinations[left].pluginRoot,
				destinations[right].pluginRoot,
			) || isInsideOrEqual(
				destinations[right].pluginRoot,
				destinations[left].pluginRoot,
			);
			if (overlaps) {
				throw new Error(
					`Overlapping deployment destinations: ${destinations[left].pluginRoot} and ${destinations[right].pluginRoot}`,
				);
			}
		}
	}

	return destinations;
}

function createPlan(destinations, projectRoot) {
	return destinations.map((destination) => {
		const files = RELEASE_FILES.map((name) => {
			const source = join(projectRoot, name);
			if (!existsSync(source) || !statSync(source).isFile()) {
				throw new Error(`Missing release file: ${source}`);
			}
			assertNoSymlinks(source);

			const target = join(destination.pluginRoot, name);
			assertNoSymlinks(target);
			const sourceHash = sha256(source);
			const targetExists = existsSync(target);
			if (targetExists && !statSync(target).isFile()) {
				throw new Error(`Deployment target is not a regular file: ${target}`);
			}
			const targetHash = targetExists ? sha256(target) : null;

			return {
				name,
				source,
				target,
				sourceHash,
				targetHash,
				changed: sourceHash !== targetHash,
			};
		});

		return { ...destination, files };
	});
}

function removeFileIfPresent(path) {
	if (existsSync(path)) unlinkSync(path);
}

function commitPlan(plan, { backup, deploymentId, dryRun, hooks = {} }) {
	const summary = plan.map((vault) => ({
		name: vault.name,
		path: vault.vaultRoot,
		pluginPath: vault.pluginRoot,
		changed: vault.files.filter((file) => file.changed).map((file) => file.name),
		unchanged: vault.files.filter((file) => !file.changed).map((file) => file.name),
		backupPath: null,
	}));

	if (dryRun) {
		return {
			dryRun: true,
			changed: summary.some((vault) => vault.changed.length > 0),
			vaults: summary,
		};
	}

	const committed = [];
	let committedFileCount = 0;

	try {
		for (const vault of plan) {
			mkdirSync(vault.pluginRoot, { recursive: true });
			assertNoSymlinks(vault.pluginRoot);
			const changed = vault.files.filter((file) => file.changed);
			if (changed.length === 0) continue;

			const durableBackup = backup
				? join(vault.pluginRoot, ".working-tabs-backups", deploymentId)
				: null;
			const rollbackRoot = join(
				vault.pluginRoot,
				`.working-tabs-rollback-${deploymentId}`,
			);
			const summaryEntry = summary.find(
				(entry) => entry.pluginPath === vault.pluginRoot,
			);

			if (durableBackup) {
				mkdirSync(durableBackup, { recursive: true });
				summaryEntry.backupPath = durableBackup;
			}
			mkdirSync(rollbackRoot, { recursive: true });

			for (const file of changed) {
				if (hooks.beforeCommit) {
					hooks.beforeCommit({
						vault,
						file,
						index: committedFileCount,
						deploymentId,
					});
				}

				const stage = join(
					vault.pluginRoot,
					`.${file.name}.working-tabs-stage-${deploymentId}`,
				);
				copyFileSync(file.source, stage);
				let rollbackPath = join(rollbackRoot, file.name);
				if (existsSync(file.target)) {
					if (durableBackup) {
						copyFileSync(file.target, join(durableBackup, file.name));
					}
					renameSync(file.target, rollbackPath);
				} else {
					rollbackPath = null;
				}

				committed.push({ file, stage, rollbackPath, rollbackRoot });
				try {
					renameSync(stage, file.target);
					committedFileCount++;
				} catch (error) {
					removeFileIfPresent(stage);
					throw error;
				}
			}
		}
	} catch (error) {
		const failures = [];
		for (const entry of committed.reverse()) {
			try {
				removeFileIfPresent(entry.file.target);
				if (entry.rollbackPath && existsSync(entry.rollbackPath)) {
					renameSync(entry.rollbackPath, entry.file.target);
				}
				removeFileIfPresent(entry.stage);
			} catch (rollbackError) {
				failures.push(
					`${entry.file.target}: ${
						rollbackError instanceof Error
							? rollbackError.message
							: String(rollbackError)
					}`,
				);
			}
		}

		for (const vault of plan) {
			const rollbackRoot = join(
				vault.pluginRoot,
				`.working-tabs-rollback-${deploymentId}`,
			);
			if (existsSync(rollbackRoot)) {
				try {
					rmdirSync(rollbackRoot);
				} catch (cleanupError) {
					failures.push(
						`${rollbackRoot}: ${
							cleanupError instanceof Error
								? cleanupError.message
								: String(cleanupError)
						}`,
					);
				}
			}
		}

		const suffix = failures.length
			? ` Rollback also failed for: ${failures.join("; ")}`
			: " All completed writes were rolled back.";
		throw new Error(
			`${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}${suffix}`,
		);
	}

	for (const entry of committed) {
		removeFileIfPresent(entry.stage);
		if (entry.rollbackPath) removeFileIfPresent(entry.rollbackPath);
	}
	for (const vault of plan) {
		const rollbackRoot = join(
			vault.pluginRoot,
			`.working-tabs-rollback-${deploymentId}`,
		);
		if (existsSync(rollbackRoot)) rmdirSync(rollbackRoot);
	}

	return {
		dryRun: false,
		changed: summary.some((vault) => vault.changed.length > 0),
		vaults: summary,
	};
}

export function deployRelease(options = {}) {
	const projectRoot = resolve(options.projectRoot ?? PROJECT_ROOT);
	assertNoSymlinks(projectRoot);
	const config = options.configPath ? readConfig(options.configPath, projectRoot) : null;
	const environment = options.environment ?? process.env;
	const vaults = parseVaults(config, options.vaults ?? [], environment);
	const backup = config?.backup ?? options.backup ?? true;
	if (typeof backup !== "boolean") throw new Error("Backup option must be boolean.");

	const manifest = readManifest(projectRoot);
	const destinations = preflightDestinations(vaults, manifest.id, projectRoot);
	if (!options.skipBuild) buildRelease(projectRoot);
	const plan = createPlan(destinations, projectRoot);
	const deploymentId = options.deploymentId ?? `deploy-${Date.now()}-${process.pid}`;
	if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$/.test(deploymentId)) {
		throw new Error("Deployment identifier is not safe.");
	}

	return commitPlan(plan, {
		backup,
		deploymentId,
		dryRun: Boolean(options.dryRun),
		hooks: options.hooks,
	});
}

export function parseArguments(argumentsList) {
	const options = {
		configPath: null,
		vaults: [],
		dryRun: false,
		skipBuild: false,
	};

	for (let index = 0; index < argumentsList.length; index++) {
		const argument = argumentsList[index];
		if (argument === "--dry-run") options.dryRun = true;
		else if (argument === "--skip-build") options.skipBuild = true;
		else if (argument === "--config") {
			const value = argumentsList[++index];
			if (!value) throw new Error("--config requires a path.");
			options.configPath = value;
		} else if (argument === "--vault") {
			const value = argumentsList[++index];
			if (!value) throw new Error("--vault requires a path.");
			options.vaults.push(value);
		} else if (argument === "--help" || argument === "-h") options.help = true;
		else throw new Error(`Unknown argument: ${argument}`);
	}

	return options;
}

const LOCAL_CONFIG_NAME = "working-tabs-deploy.local.json";

function usage() {
	console.log(
		"Usage: node scripts/deploy.mjs [--config path] [--vault path ...] [--dry-run] [--skip-build]",
	);
	console.log(
		`With no --config and no --vault, ${LOCAL_CONFIG_NAME} is used when it exists.`,
	);
}

if (
	process.argv[1]
	&& resolve(process.argv[1]) === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)
) {
	try {
		const options = parseArguments(process.argv.slice(2));
		if (!options.configPath && options.vaults.length === 0) {
			const localConfig = join(PROJECT_ROOT, LOCAL_CONFIG_NAME);
			if (existsSync(localConfig)) options.configPath = localConfig;
		}
		if (options.help) usage();
		else console.log(JSON.stringify(deployRelease(options), null, 2));
	} catch (error) {
		console.error(error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error));
		process.exitCode = 1;
	}
}

```
# Working tabs

<p align="center">
  <a href="https://github.com/NoteNerdOfficial/working-tabs/commits/main"><img src="https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/NoteNerdOfficial/working-tabs?style=flat-square" alt="last commit"></a>
  <a href="https://github.com/NoteNerdOfficial/working-tabs/releases/latest"><img src="https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/NoteNerdOfficial/working-tabs?style=flat-square&label=release" alt="release"></a>
  <a href="https://obsidian.md/plugins?id=working-tabs"><img src="https://img.shields.io/badge/dynamic/json?style=flat-square&logo=obsidian&color=7C3AED&label=downloads&query=%24%5B%22working-tabs%22%5D.downloads&url=https%3A%2F%2Fraw.githubusercontent.com%2Fobsidianmd%2Fobsidian-releases%2Fmaster%2Fcommunity-plugin-stats.json" alt="Obsidian downloads"></a>
</p>

Your open tabs, organized by what you're working on *right now* — not by folder, and not by layout. Inspired by Workona, built for Obsidian.

<p align="center">
  <img src="docs/demo.gif" width="840" alt="The Working tabs sidebar beside three Obsidian panes. Groups are browsed and their tabs focused, then checked off one at a time until a group completes itself into Completed; a new section is created, renamed, and groups are dragged into it.">
</p>

**Colour-code your groups and sections too.** Every one is auto-assigned a colour, drawn as a stripe down its pane's left edge and a matching bar on its sidebar row — so you can tell at a glance which pane belongs where. File a group into a section and it takes on that section's colour.

<p align="center">
  <img src="docs/colour-coding.gif" width="840" alt="A colour is picked for a group from its menu, showing the palette with a swatch beside each name. A new section is then created and a group dragged into it, which immediately takes on the section's colour.">
</p>

## Why

Arranging *how* open tabs render — columns, continuous scroll, and the like — is a layout problem. It doesn't solve the actual one: **you have twelve tabs open across three panes and no way to say "these six belong together, tuck them away, and give me back my screen."**

Working tabs is task-and-timeframe oriented, not layout-oriented:

- **Tabs-as-tasks.** A tab stays open because the work behind it isn't done. So a group of tabs is a unit of in-progress work, not just a pile of panes — closing it out is *completing* it, and completed groups sit in a recoverable Completed list instead of just vanishing.
- **Timeframe over project.** Your notes are already organized by project or topic — that's what your vault's folders and links are for. What they don't capture is *when* something matters: this week's research, a deadline you're heads-down on, a sprint that ends Friday. Sections exist for that — a place to park related groups for as long as they're relevant, then hide the whole thing in one click once the timeframe's over, without deleting anything.
- **Every pane is already a group.** There's no "create a group" step to remember. Open some tabs in a pane and Working tabs has already named it, tracked it, and listed it in the sidebar — organizing it into a section or renaming it is optional, not required up front.

## In practice

Two shapes this tends to take:

**Notes, by timeframe.** A section per sprint, deadline, or research push; the groups inside it are the threads of work you're actually holding open. When the timeframe ends, hide the section and the whole thing goes quiet in one click.

**Terminals, by what they're doing.** If you run terminals in your vault — say with [Terminus](https://community.obsidian.md/plugins/terminus) — they pile up fast, and they aren't interchangeable. Three long-lived Claude Code sessions you're actively talking to are a different kind of thing from the throwaway shells running `npx expo run:ios` or `astro build`. Put each kind in its own pane and you already have two groups: one you keep in view, one you hide until a build fails.

Hiding matters here specifically because it doesn't close anything — the pane is tucked out of sight, not torn down, so every process inside it keeps running while you get the screen space back. (Completing a group *does* close its pane, which ends whatever was running in it.) Terminal tabs are tracked for as long as Obsidian stays open; unlike note tabs, they can't be reopened after a restart, since the underlying processes don't survive one either.

## Features

### Groups
- Every pane of tabs in the main workspace is automatically a group — no manual creation step.
- Hover a group for quick actions: hide the pane, mark it complete, or open its menu. Click the row to reveal its pane if it's already open, or reopen it if it's dormant.
- **Open in...** split right, split down, new window, or new tab — matching Obsidian's own placement vocabulary. Opening into an already-occupied pane merges the two groups together.
- Rename inline (double-click or F2) and add an optional description shown under the title.
- **Hide a group** to tuck its pane away without closing it — the tabs stay open in the background, just out of view, and unhiding brings them right back.
- **Colour coding** ties a pane to its place in the sidebar: every group and section is auto-assigned a colour, drawn as a stripe down the pane's left edge and a matching bar on the sidebar row. Groups follow their section's colour, so filing a group into a section adopts it — even one you'd recoloured by hand — and dragging it back out restores its own. Pick "Colour" on any group or section to override, "No colour" to opt one out, or "Automatic" to go back to following along. Turn the whole thing off in settings without losing the colours you picked.
- **Closing a pane never deletes its group** — whether you use the sidebar's "Close group" or Obsidian's own tab-strip menu ("Close all", closing the last tab, closing the split), the group just goes dormant with its tab list intact, ready to reopen. Deleting it is always a deliberate choice.
- **Complete a group** when the work is done: its pane closes, but the group and its tab list move to Completed, fully restorable later. A per-tab "done" checkbox lets you check off individual tabs without completing the whole group.

<p align="center">
  <img src="docs/demo-sidebar.gif" width="330" alt="The sidebar panel. Three tabs are checked off one by one, each striking through and dropping to the bottom of its group; with all three done the group leaves the list and lands under Completed. A new section is then created, renamed, and groups are dragged into it.">
  <br>
  <em>Check tabs off as you finish them — the group completes itself and moves to Completed. Sections keep what's left filed by timeframe.</em>
</p>

### Sections
- Fold related groups together under one collapsible header — by timeframe, sprint, or whatever grouping makes sense for how you work.
- **Hide a section** to tuck away every group inside it at once, without touching each group's own hidden state — unhiding the section restores exactly what was hidden before.
- Sections always sort below your ungrouped, currently-open groups, so the top of the panel stays focused on what's live right now.

### Everything else
- **Drag and drop** to reorder groups, move tabs between groups, or file groups into sections.
- **Search** across tab and group titles, auto-expanding whatever matches.
- **Keyboard navigation**: arrow keys to move, Enter to open, F2 to rename, Delete to remove.
- **Restart-safe**: reopens matching tabs by file path after Obsidian restarts, and follows file renames so a group never silently loses track of a note.
- **Beyond notes**: tracks any pane — Terminus terminals, the Web Viewer, canvases, any other plugin's view — not just files. Titles set by another plugin's own UI (renaming a terminal tab, a browser tab's title loading in) are picked up too.

## Commands

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| Open sidebar | Reveals the Working tabs panel |
| Toggle hide tab bar | Quick on/off for the "Hide tab bar" appearance setting, without opening Settings |

## Settings

| Setting | Description |
|---|---|
| Confirm before completing a group | Ask before marking a group done. Turn off once you trust it — completed groups can still be restored |
| Long titles | Truncate titles and descriptions with an ellipsis, or wrap them to multiple lines |
| Colour code groups and sections | Show each group's colour as a stripe on its pane and a bar in the sidebar. Off hides every stripe without forgetting your picks |
| Hide tab bar | Hide Obsidian's native tab-header row across every pane, for a cleaner look |

## Installation

1. Open **Settings → Community plugins** in Obsidian.
2. Click **Browse**, search for **Working tabs**, and click **Install**.
3. Click **Enable**. The panel opens in the left sidebar the first time you turn it on.

## Development

```bash
npm install
npm run dev    # watch mode with source maps
npm run build  # production bundle
```

## Deploy from source

Copy the example deployment config to an ignored local file:

```bash
cp working-tabs-deploy.example.json working-tabs-deploy.local.json
```

On Windows PowerShell, use:

```powershell
Copy-Item .\working-tabs-deploy.example.json .\working-tabs-deploy.local.json
```

Edit `working-tabs-deploy.local.json` and set each vault's `path` and `enabled` value:

```json
{
  "$schema": "./deploy-config.schema.json",
  "backup": true,
  "vaults": [
    {
      "name": "Primary",
      "path": "D:/Vaults/Primary",
      "enabled": true
    }
  ]
}
```

Forward slashes are recommended in Windows JSON paths. If you use backslashes, JSON requires each one to be doubled, for example `D:\\Vaults\\Primary`.

`npm run deploy` reads `working-tabs-deploy.local.json` when that file exists. Preview the deployment first, then run it:

```bash
npm run deploy -- --dry-run
npm run deploy
```

You can also deploy without a config file:

```bash
npm run deploy -- --vault "D:/Vaults/Primary" --vault "D:/Vaults/Test"
```

The deployer builds once, validates every vault before writing, and copies only `main.js`, `manifest.json`, and `styles.css` into `.obsidian/plugins/working-tabs/`. It skips unchanged files, preserves `data.json` and unrelated files, creates backups for changed release files, and rolls back completed writes if a multi-vault deployment fails. Every path must point to an existing Obsidian vault containing `.obsidian`; symbolic links, duplicate destinations, and paths overlapping the source repository are rejected.

The user is asking why I put `--` between arguments when running npm scripts, like `npm run deploy -- --dry-run`.

The `--` is npm's separator. It tells npm to pass everything after it directly to the script. Without it, npm might try to interpret those arguments as its own options.

The user seems frustrated by the extra `--` in the commands I provided. They likely just want to run `npm run deploy` without passing any flags.

The `--` is only needed when passing flags to the script. A plain `npm run deploy` does not require it. I should explain this briefly and directly.

The `--` belongs to npm, not to the deploy script. It marks the end of npm's own arguments. Everything after it is handed to `scripts/deploy.mjs`.

```bash
npm run deploy -- --dry-run
```

That runs `node scripts/deploy.mjs --dry-run`. Without the separator, npm treats `--dry-run` as one of its own options and the script never sees it.

A plain deploy has nothing to pass through, so there is no separator:

```bash
npm run deploy
```

import {
	accessSync,
	constants,
	copyFileSync,
	existsSync,
	lstatSync,
	mkdirSync,
	readFileSync,
	renameSync,
	rmdirSync,
	statSync,
	unlinkSync,
} from "node:fs";
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
import {
	dirname,
	isAbsolute,
	join,
	parse,
	relative,
	resolve,
	sep,
} from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

const RELEASE_FILES = Object.freeze(["main.js", "manifest.json", "styles.css"]);
export const PROJECT_ROOT = resolve(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");

function isInsideOrEqual(parent, child) {
	const relation = relative(parent, child);
	return relation === ""
		|| (!relation.startsWith(`..${sep}`) && relation !== ".." && !isAbsolute(relation));
}

function assertNoSymlinks(candidate) {
	const absolute = resolve(candidate);
	const root = parse(absolute).root;
	let current = root;

	for (const component of relative(root, absolute).split(sep).filter(Boolean)) {
		current = join(current, component);
		if (!existsSync(current)) continue;
		if (lstatSync(current).isSymbolicLink()) {
			throw new Error(`Symbolic links are not allowed in deployment paths: ${current}`);
		}
	}
}

function expandEnvironment(value, environment) {
	return value.replace(/\$\{([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\}/g, (_match, name) => {
		const replacement = environment[name];
		if (replacement === undefined) {
			throw new Error(
				`Environment variable ${name} is required by the deployment configuration.`,
			);
		}
		return replacement;
	});
}

function readStrictJson(path, description) {
	assertNoSymlinks(path);
	if (!existsSync(path) || !statSync(path).isFile()) {
		throw new Error(`${description} does not exist: ${path}`);
	}

	try {
		return JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, "utf8"));
	} catch (error) {
		const detail = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
		const windowsHint = process.platform === "win32"
			? " On Windows, use forward slashes or double every backslash in paths."
			: "";
		throw new Error(`${description} is not strict JSON: ${path} (${detail}).${windowsHint}`);
	}
}

function readManifest(projectRoot) {
	const manifestPath = join(projectRoot, "manifest.json");
	const manifest = readStrictJson(manifestPath, "Plugin manifest");
	if (!manifest || typeof manifest !== "object" || Array.isArray(manifest)) {
		throw new Error("Plugin manifest must be a JSON object.");
	}
	if (typeof manifest.id !== "string" || !/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/.test(manifest.id)) {
		throw new Error("Plugin manifest has an invalid id.");
	}
	return manifest;
}

function strictConfig(value) {
	if (!value || typeof value !== "object" || Array.isArray(value)) {
		throw new Error("Deployment config must be a JSON object.");
	}

	const allowed = new Set(["$schema", "vaults", "backup"]);
	for (const key of Object.keys(value)) {
		if (!allowed.has(key)) throw new Error(`Unknown config property: ${key}`);
	}
	if (value.$schema !== undefined && typeof value.$schema !== "string") {
		throw new Error('Config property "$schema" must be a string.');
	}
	if (typeof value.backup !== "boolean") {
		throw new Error('Config property "backup" must be boolean.');
	}
	if (!Array.isArray(value.vaults) || value.vaults.length === 0) {
		throw new Error('Config property "vaults" must be a non-empty array.');
	}
	return value;
}

function parseVaults(config, vaultArgs, environment) {
	const configured = config
		? strictConfig(config).vaults.map((entry) => {
			if (!entry || typeof entry !== "object" || Array.isArray(entry)) {
				throw new Error("Each vault must be an object.");
			}

			const allowed = new Set(["name", "path", "enabled"]);
			for (const key of Object.keys(entry)) {
				if (!allowed.has(key)) throw new Error(`Unknown vault property: ${key}`);
			}
			if (typeof entry.name !== "string" || !entry.name.trim()) {
				throw new Error("Each vault requires a non-empty name.");
			}
			if (typeof entry.path !== "string" || !entry.path.trim()) {
				throw new Error("Each vault requires a non-empty path.");
			}
			if (typeof entry.enabled !== "boolean") {
				throw new Error("Each vault requires an enabled boolean.");
			}

			const name = expandEnvironment(entry.name, environment);
			const path = expandEnvironment(entry.path, environment);
			if (!name.trim() || !path.trim()) {
				throw new Error("Expanded vault names and paths must be non-empty.");
			}
			return { name, path, enabled: entry.enabled };
		})
		: [];

	const overrides = vaultArgs.map((vaultPath, index) => ({
		name: `Command-line vault ${index + 1}`,
		path: expandEnvironment(vaultPath, environment),
		enabled: true,
	}));

	return configured.concat(overrides).filter((vault) => vault.enabled);
}

function readConfig(configPath, projectRoot) {
	if (!configPath) return null;
	const absolute = isAbsolute(configPath)
		? resolve(configPath)
		: resolve(projectRoot, configPath);
	return readStrictJson(absolute, "Deployment config");
}

function sha256(path) {
	return createHash("sha256").update(readFileSync(path)).digest("hex");
}

function buildRelease(projectRoot) {
	const bundledNpmCli = join(
		dirname(process.execPath),
		"node_modules",
		"npm",
		"bin",
		"npm-cli.js",
	);
	const npmExecPath = process.env.npm_execpath;
	let executable = process.execPath;
	let argumentsList;

	if (npmExecPath && existsSync(npmExecPath) && /\.(?:c?js)$/.test(npmExecPath)) {
		argumentsList = [npmExecPath, "run", "build"];
	} else if (existsSync(bundledNpmCli)) {
		argumentsList = [bundledNpmCli, "run", "build"];
	} else if (process.platform !== "win32") {
		executable = "npm";
		argumentsList = ["run", "build"];
	} else {
		throw new Error("Could not resolve the npm CLI without a shell command.");
	}

	const result = spawnSync(executable, argumentsList, {
		cwd: projectRoot,
		stdio: "inherit",
		shell: false,
	});
	if (result.error) throw new Error(`Build failed: ${result.error.message}`);
	if (result.status !== 0) {
		throw new Error(`Build failed with exit code ${result.status ?? "unknown"}.`);
	}
}

function preflightDestinations(vaults, pluginId, projectRoot) {
	if (vaults.length === 0) throw new Error("No enabled vaults were configured.");

	const destinations = vaults.map((vault) => {
		const vaultRoot = isAbsolute(vault.path)
			? resolve(vault.path)
			: resolve(projectRoot, vault.path);
		assertNoSymlinks(vaultRoot);
		if (!existsSync(vaultRoot) || !statSync(vaultRoot).isDirectory()) {
			throw new Error(`Vault does not exist: ${vaultRoot}`);
		}

		const configDirectory = join(vaultRoot, ".obsidian");
		assertNoSymlinks(configDirectory);
		if (!existsSync(configDirectory) || !statSync(configDirectory).isDirectory()) {
			throw new Error(
				`Path is not an Obsidian vault because .obsidian is missing: ${vaultRoot}`,
			);
		}
		accessSync(configDirectory, constants.R_OK | constants.W_OK);

		const pluginRoot = join(configDirectory, "plugins", pluginId);
		assertNoSymlinks(pluginRoot);
		const overlapsProject = isInsideOrEqual(projectRoot, pluginRoot)
			|| isInsideOrEqual(pluginRoot, projectRoot);
		if (overlapsProject) {
			throw new Error(`Unsafe deployment destination overlaps the project source: ${pluginRoot}`);
		}

		return { ...vault, vaultRoot, pluginRoot, files: [] };
	});

	for (let left = 0; left < destinations.length; left++) {
		for (let right = left + 1; right < destinations.length; right++) {
			const overlaps = isInsideOrEqual(
				destinations[left].pluginRoot,
				destinations[right].pluginRoot,
			) || isInsideOrEqual(
				destinations[right].pluginRoot,
				destinations[left].pluginRoot,
			);
			if (overlaps) {
				throw new Error(
					`Overlapping deployment destinations: ${destinations[left].pluginRoot} and ${destinations[right].pluginRoot}`,
				);
			}
		}
	}

	return destinations;
}

function createPlan(destinations, projectRoot) {
	return destinations.map((destination) => {
		const files = RELEASE_FILES.map((name) => {
			const source = join(projectRoot, name);
			if (!existsSync(source) || !statSync(source).isFile()) {
				throw new Error(`Missing release file: ${source}`);
			}
			assertNoSymlinks(source);

			const target = join(destination.pluginRoot, name);
			assertNoSymlinks(target);
			const sourceHash = sha256(source);
			const targetExists = existsSync(target);
			if (targetExists && !statSync(target).isFile()) {
				throw new Error(`Deployment target is not a regular file: ${target}`);
			}
			const targetHash = targetExists ? sha256(target) : null;

			return {
				name,
				source,
				target,
				sourceHash,
				targetHash,
				changed: sourceHash !== targetHash,
			};
		});

		return { ...destination, files };
	});
}

function removeFileIfPresent(path) {
	if (existsSync(path)) unlinkSync(path);
}

function commitPlan(plan, { backup, deploymentId, dryRun, hooks = {} }) {
	const summary = plan.map((vault) => ({
		name: vault.name,
		path: vault.vaultRoot,
		pluginPath: vault.pluginRoot,
		changed: vault.files.filter((file) => file.changed).map((file) => file.name),
		unchanged: vault.files.filter((file) => !file.changed).map((file) => file.name),
		backupPath: null,
	}));

	if (dryRun) {
		return {
			dryRun: true,
			changed: summary.some((vault) => vault.changed.length > 0),
			vaults: summary,
		};
	}

	const committed = [];
	let committedFileCount = 0;

	try {
		for (const vault of plan) {
			mkdirSync(vault.pluginRoot, { recursive: true });
			assertNoSymlinks(vault.pluginRoot);
			const changed = vault.files.filter((file) => file.changed);
			if (changed.length === 0) continue;

			const durableBackup = backup
				? join(vault.pluginRoot, ".working-tabs-backups", deploymentId)
				: null;
			const rollbackRoot = join(
				vault.pluginRoot,
				`.working-tabs-rollback-${deploymentId}`,
			);
			const summaryEntry = summary.find(
				(entry) => entry.pluginPath === vault.pluginRoot,
			);

			if (durableBackup) {
				mkdirSync(durableBackup, { recursive: true });
				summaryEntry.backupPath = durableBackup;
			}
			mkdirSync(rollbackRoot, { recursive: true });

			for (const file of changed) {
				if (hooks.beforeCommit) {
					hooks.beforeCommit({
						vault,
						file,
						index: committedFileCount,
						deploymentId,
					});
				}

				const stage = join(
					vault.pluginRoot,
					`.${file.name}.working-tabs-stage-${deploymentId}`,
				);
				copyFileSync(file.source, stage);
				let rollbackPath = join(rollbackRoot, file.name);
				if (existsSync(file.target)) {
					if (durableBackup) {
						copyFileSync(file.target, join(durableBackup, file.name));
					}
					renameSync(file.target, rollbackPath);
				} else {
					rollbackPath = null;
				}

				committed.push({ file, stage, rollbackPath, rollbackRoot });
				try {
					renameSync(stage, file.target);
					committedFileCount++;
				} catch (error) {
					removeFileIfPresent(stage);
					throw error;
				}
			}
		}
	} catch (error) {
		const failures = [];
		for (const entry of committed.reverse()) {
			try {
				removeFileIfPresent(entry.file.target);
				if (entry.rollbackPath && existsSync(entry.rollbackPath)) {
					renameSync(entry.rollbackPath, entry.file.target);
				}
				removeFileIfPresent(entry.stage);
			} catch (rollbackError) {
				failures.push(
					`${entry.file.target}: ${
						rollbackError instanceof Error
							? rollbackError.message
							: String(rollbackError)
					}`,
				);
			}
		}

		for (const vault of plan) {
			const rollbackRoot = join(
				vault.pluginRoot,
				`.working-tabs-rollback-${deploymentId}`,
			);
			if (existsSync(rollbackRoot)) {
				try {
					rmdirSync(rollbackRoot);
				} catch (cleanupError) {
					failures.push(
						`${rollbackRoot}: ${
							cleanupError instanceof Error
								? cleanupError.message
								: String(cleanupError)
						}`,
					);
				}
			}
		}

		const suffix = failures.length
			? ` Rollback also failed for: ${failures.join("; ")}`
			: " All completed writes were rolled back.";
		throw new Error(
			`${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}${suffix}`,
		);
	}

	for (const entry of committed) {
		removeFileIfPresent(entry.stage);
		if (entry.rollbackPath) removeFileIfPresent(entry.rollbackPath);
	}
	for (const vault of plan) {
		const rollbackRoot = join(
			vault.pluginRoot,
			`.working-tabs-rollback-${deploymentId}`,
		);
		if (existsSync(rollbackRoot)) rmdirSync(rollbackRoot);
	}

	return {
		dryRun: false,
		changed: summary.some((vault) => vault.changed.length > 0),
		vaults: summary,
	};
}

export function deployRelease(options = {}) {
	const projectRoot = resolve(options.projectRoot ?? PROJECT_ROOT);
	assertNoSymlinks(projectRoot);
	const config = options.configPath ? readConfig(options.configPath, projectRoot) : null;
	const environment = options.environment ?? process.env;
	const vaults = parseVaults(config, options.vaults ?? [], environment);
	const backup = config?.backup ?? options.backup ?? true;
	if (typeof backup !== "boolean") throw new Error("Backup option must be boolean.");

	const manifest = readManifest(projectRoot);
	const destinations = preflightDestinations(vaults, manifest.id, projectRoot);
	if (!options.skipBuild) buildRelease(projectRoot);
	const plan = createPlan(destinations, projectRoot);
	const deploymentId = options.deploymentId ?? `deploy-${Date.now()}-${process.pid}`;
	if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$/.test(deploymentId)) {
		throw new Error("Deployment identifier is not safe.");
	}

	return commitPlan(plan, {
		backup,
		deploymentId,
		dryRun: Boolean(options.dryRun),
		hooks: options.hooks,
	});
}

export function parseArguments(argumentsList) {
	const options = {
		configPath: null,
		vaults: [],
		dryRun: false,
		skipBuild: false,
	};

	for (let index = 0; index < argumentsList.length; index++) {
		const argument = argumentsList[index];
		if (argument === "--dry-run") options.dryRun = true;
		else if (argument === "--skip-build") options.skipBuild = true;
		else if (argument === "--config") {
			const value = argumentsList[++index];
			if (!value) throw new Error("--config requires a path.");
			options.configPath = value;
		} else if (argument === "--vault") {
			const value = argumentsList[++index];
			if (!value) throw new Error("--vault requires a path.");
			options.vaults.push(value);
		} else if (argument === "--help" || argument === "-h") options.help = true;
		else throw new Error(`Unknown argument: ${argument}`);
	}

	return options;
}

function usage() {
	console.log(
		"Usage: node scripts/deploy.mjs [--config path] [--vault path ...] [--dry-run] [--skip-build]",
	);
}

if (
	process.argv[1]
	&& resolve(process.argv[1]) === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)
) {
	try {
		const options = parseArguments(process.argv.slice(2));
		if (options.help) usage();
		else console.log(JSON.stringify(deployRelease(options), null, 2));
	} catch (error) {
		console.error(error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error));
		process.exitCode = 1;
	}
}

```

# Working tabs

<p align="center">
  <a href="https://github.com/NoteNerdOfficial/working-tabs/commits/main"><img src="https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/NoteNerdOfficial/working-tabs?style=flat-square" alt="last commit"></a>
  <a href="https://github.com/NoteNerdOfficial/working-tabs/releases/latest"><img src="https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/NoteNerdOfficial/working-tabs?style=flat-square&label=release" alt="release"></a>
  <a href="https://obsidian.md/plugins?id=working-tabs"><img src="https://img.shields.io/badge/dynamic/json?style=flat-square&logo=obsidian&color=7C3AED&label=downloads&query=%24%5B%22working-tabs%22%5D.downloads&url=https%3A%2F%2Fraw.githubusercontent.com%2Fobsidianmd%2Fobsidian-releases%2Fmaster%2Fcommunity-plugin-stats.json" alt="Obsidian downloads"></a>
</p>

Your open tabs, organized by what you're working on *right now* — not by folder, and not by layout. Inspired by Workona, built for Obsidian.

<p align="center">
  <img src="docs/demo.gif" width="840" alt="The Working tabs sidebar beside three Obsidian panes. Groups are browsed and their tabs focused, then checked off one at a time until a group completes itself into Completed; a new section is created, renamed, and groups are dragged into it.">
</p>

**Colour-code your groups and sections too.** Every one is auto-assigned a colour, drawn as a stripe down its pane's left edge and a matching bar on its sidebar row — so you can tell at a glance which pane belongs where. File a group into a section and it takes on that section's colour.

<p align="center">
  <img src="docs/colour-coding.gif" width="840" alt="A colour is picked for a group from its menu, showing the palette with a swatch beside each name. A new section is then created and a group dragged into it, which immediately takes on the section's colour.">
</p>

## Why

Arranging *how* open tabs render — columns, continuous scroll, and the like — is a layout problem. It doesn't solve the actual one: **you have twelve tabs open across three panes and no way to say "these six belong together, tuck them away, and give me back my screen."**

Working tabs is task-and-timeframe oriented, not layout-oriented:

- **Tabs-as-tasks.** A tab stays open because the work behind it isn't done. So a group of tabs is a unit of in-progress work, not just a pile of panes — closing it out is *completing* it, and completed groups sit in a recoverable Completed list instead of just vanishing.
- **Timeframe over project.** Your notes are already organized by project or topic — that's what your vault's folders and links are for. What they don't capture is *when* something matters: this week's research, a deadline you're heads-down on, a sprint that ends Friday. Sections exist for that — a place to park related groups for as long as they're relevant, then hide the whole thing in one click once the timeframe's over, without deleting anything.
- **Every pane is already a group.** There's no "create a group" step to remember. Open some tabs in a pane and Working tabs has already named it, tracked it, and listed it in the sidebar — organizing it into a section or renaming it is optional, not required up front.

## In practice

Two shapes this tends to take:

**Notes, by timeframe.** A section per sprint, deadline, or research push; the groups inside it are the threads of work you're actually holding open. When the timeframe ends, hide the section and the whole thing goes quiet in one click.

**Terminals, by what they're doing.** If you run terminals in your vault — say with [Terminus](https://community.obsidian.md/plugins/terminus) — they pile up fast, and they aren't interchangeable. Three long-lived Claude Code sessions you're actively talking to are a different kind of thing from the throwaway shells running `npx expo run:ios` or `astro build`. Put each kind in its own pane and you already have two groups: one you keep in view, one you hide until a build fails.

Hiding matters here specifically because it doesn't close anything — the pane is tucked out of sight, not torn down, so every process inside it keeps running while you get the screen space back. (Completing a group *does* close its pane, which ends whatever was running in it.) Terminal tabs are tracked for as long as Obsidian stays open; unlike note tabs, they can't be reopened after a restart, since the underlying processes don't survive one either.

## Features

### Groups
- Every pane of tabs in the main workspace is automatically a group — no manual creation step.
- Hover a group for quick actions: hide the pane, mark it complete, or open its menu. Click the row to reveal its pane if it's already open, or reopen it if it's dormant.
- **Open in...** split right, split down, new window, or new tab — matching Obsidian's own placement vocabulary. Opening into an already-occupied pane merges the two groups together.
- Rename inline (double-click or F2) and add an optional description shown under the title.
- **Hide a group** to tuck its pane away without closing it — the tabs stay open in the background, just out of view, and unhiding brings them right back.
- **Colour coding** ties a pane to its place in the sidebar: every group and section is auto-assigned a colour, drawn as a stripe down the pane's left edge and a matching bar on the sidebar row. Groups follow their section's colour, so filing a group into a section adopts it — even one you'd recoloured by hand — and dragging it back out restores its own. Pick "Colour" on any group or section to override, "No colour" to opt one out, or "Automatic" to go back to following along. Turn the whole thing off in settings without losing the colours you picked.
- **Closing a pane never deletes its group** — whether you use the sidebar's "Close group" or Obsidian's own tab-strip menu ("Close all", closing the last tab, closing the split), the group just goes dormant with its tab list intact, ready to reopen. Deleting it is always a deliberate choice.
- **Complete a group** when the work is done: its pane closes, but the group and its tab list move to Completed, fully restorable later. A per-tab "done" checkbox lets you check off individual tabs without completing the whole group.

<p align="center">
  <img src="docs/demo-sidebar.gif" width="330" alt="The sidebar panel. Three tabs are checked off one by one, each striking through and dropping to the bottom of its group; with all three done the group leaves the list and lands under Completed. A new section is then created, renamed, and groups are dragged into it.">
  <br>
  <em>Check tabs off as you finish them — the group completes itself and moves to Completed. Sections keep what's left filed by timeframe.</em>
</p>

### Sections
- Fold related groups together under one collapsible header — by timeframe, sprint, or whatever grouping makes sense for how you work.
- **Hide a section** to tuck away every group inside it at once, without touching each group's own hidden state — unhiding the section restores exactly what was hidden before.
- Sections always sort below your ungrouped, currently-open groups, so the top of the panel stays focused on what's live right now.

### Everything else
- **Drag and drop** to reorder groups, move tabs between groups, or file groups into sections.
- **Search** across tab and group titles, auto-expanding whatever matches.
- **Keyboard navigation**: arrow keys to move, Enter to open, F2 to rename, Delete to remove.
- **Restart-safe**: reopens matching tabs by file path after Obsidian restarts, and follows file renames so a group never silently loses track of a note.
- **Beyond notes**: tracks any pane — Terminus terminals, the Web Viewer, canvases, any other plugin's view — not just files. Titles set by another plugin's own UI (renaming a terminal tab, a browser tab's title loading in) are picked up too.

## Commands

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| Open sidebar | Reveals the Working tabs panel |
| Toggle hide tab bar | Quick on/off for the "Hide tab bar" appearance setting, without opening Settings |

## Settings

| Setting | Description |
|---|---|
| Confirm before completing a group | Ask before marking a group done. Turn off once you trust it — completed groups can still be restored |
| Long titles | Truncate titles and descriptions with an ellipsis, or wrap them to multiple lines |
| Colour code groups and sections | Show each group's colour as a stripe on its pane and a bar in the sidebar. Off hides every stripe without forgetting your picks |
| Hide tab bar | Hide Obsidian's native tab-header row across every pane, for a cleaner look |

## Installation

1. Open **Settings → Community plugins** in Obsidian.
2. Click **Browse**, search for **Working tabs**, and click **Install**.
3. Click **Enable**. The panel opens in the left sidebar the first time you turn it on.

## Development

```bash
npm install
npm run dev    # watch mode with source maps
npm run build  # production bundle
```

## Deploy from source

Copy the example deployment config to an ignored local file:

```bash
cp working-tabs-deploy.example.json working-tabs-deploy.local.json
```

On Windows PowerShell, use:

```powershell
Copy-Item .\working-tabs-deploy.example.json .\working-tabs-deploy.local.json
```

Edit `working-tabs-deploy.local.json` and set each vault's `path` and `enabled` value:

```json
{
  "$schema": "./deploy-config.schema.json",
  "backup": true,
  "vaults": [
    {
      "name": "Primary",
      "path": "D:/Vaults/Primary",
      "enabled": true
    }
  ]
}
```

Forward slashes are recommended in Windows JSON paths. If you use backslashes, JSON requires each one to be doubled, for example `D:\\Vaults\\Primary`.

`npm run deploy` passes `working-tabs-deploy.local.json` for you. Preview the deployment first, then run it:

```bash
npm run deploy -- --dry-run
npm run deploy
```

You can also deploy without a config file:

```bash
npm run deploy -- --vault "D:/Vaults/Primary" --vault "D:/Vaults/Test"
```

The deployer builds once, validates every vault before writing, and copies only `main.js`, `manifest.json`, and `styles.css` into `.obsidian/plugins/working-tabs/`. It skips unchanged files, preserves `data.json` and unrelated files, creates backups for changed release files, and rolls back completed writes if a multi-vault deployment fails. Every path must point to an existing Obsidian vault containing `.obsidian`; symbolic links, duplicate destinations, and paths overlapping the source repository are rejected.

## License

MIT, see [LICENSE](LICENSE).
