This is a substantial feature. Let me design the minimal correct implementation.

Designing the pool model. A tab in a pool has specific properties.

Pooled tabs store `originGroupId` and `originOrder` while keeping `parentId` as the section id. The leaf stays open in the origin group's pane. `plan()` must skip duplicate tab additions for pooled leaves, avoid moving records back to the live group, and handle pruning correctly since pooled tabs are not children of the live group.

The mirror pass is the real bug. It finds the existing pooled tab and adds a duplicate because the leaf's origin is a section. The fix is to skip existing pooled tabs in the mirror loop. New group and addTab logic for unclaimed panes must also ignore pooled keys.

Title sync and group ordering remain unaffected by the pool. Moving a pooled tab to a group clears its pool metadata and relocates the leaf without revealing it. Reveal behavior varies by move path: relocateLiveLeaf and reopenTab do not reveal, while moveTabToNewGroup and dockTab do.

`relocateLiveLeaf` calls `selectTabIndex`, which could focus the moved tab in the target pane. That would make the view jump if the pane is visible. The send-to-group flow should avoid this to keep the view from flying.

The wireframe allows sending a tab to an off-screen group. The leaf must detach from the current pane and update its record without opening the target pane. The existing moveTab logic blocks this because it rejects targets that are not live when the leaf is open.

Sending a tab to an off-screen group closes its leaf. The record moves to the target group. The leaf reopens only when that group is shown again. The wireframe confirms the leaf leaves the visible strip and the view does not jump.

The explicit send flow must clear origin metadata when moving to a named group. For pooled tabs, the original origin group and order should be preserved so the leaf returns to its home pane.

Re-pooling a tab updates the section id but preserves the original origin group and order. The leaf stays open and is not relocated. plan() must leave it untouched. Returning to the origin group moves the tab back to its original order and clears the origin metadata. The leaf should already be in the origin pane.

Tab row clicks should only highlight the row. The existing mousedown already handles highlighting, so focusTab must be removed from the click handler. Group clicks should toggle collapse instead of selecting. The wireframe shows that selecting a group reveals it on screen or off screen, which already happens when the focusedId is set.

Obsidian 1.7+ removed the global pane menu event. Community plugins hook into the `file-menu` event and filter for `source === 'tab-header'` or `'more-options'` to add items to every tab header menu.

The `file-menu` event fires from `Workspace.handleFileContextMenu` and from markdown view tab menus when the tab has a file. Non-file tabs like terminals do not trigger it. Monkeypatching `Workspace.prototype` or `ItemView` is another possible approach.

Monkeypatching `Menu.prototype.showAtPosition` or wrapping tab headers via `layout-change` is possible but fragile. The `file-menu` event pattern is the more reliable approach.

Leaves have `tabHeaderEl`. I can map selected headers to leaves.

Starting implementation with types.ts.

SpaceNode gains `originGroupId` and `originOrder` fields. `membership.ts` gets an `isPooled` helper to detect section-pooled tabs. The mirror loop skips pooled leaves. New groups skip leaves matching pooled tabs. Title sync stays in step 1. Pooled leaves persist after being closed in Obsidian.

Pool records persist even after the native tab is closed. Reconcile will not delete them. Duplicate keys resolve to the last write.

`store.ts` will get `parkInSection` and `restoreOrigin`. `parkInSection` records the tab's origin group and order, then moves it into the section. `restoreOrigin` returns the tab to its origin group at the saved order and clears the origin fields. If the origin group no longer exists, the tab stays in the pool.

`sendToGroup` may belong in leaf-sync rather than store. `sendToPool` will park records without touching leaves. `sendToGroup` will clear origin fields, then move records into the target group and relocate live leaves. Dormant targets need leaf detachment before record movement. A new `sendTabs` helper may be needed.

`closeLiveTabOnly` cannot detach pooled tabs because their parent is a section, not a group. A new `detachOpenLeaf` helper will detach leaves by tab key regardless of parent. `sendToGroup` will use this to detach dormant targets before moving records into the group.

For live targets, `sendToGroup` will relocate the existing leaf if it is open, or reopen it if the leaf was detached. Reopening a closed leaf in a live target pane will set its view state active and focus it, but this is acceptable because the target is already on screen.

Drag-and-drop will route tabs into sections to `sendToPool` instead of the old `moveTab`. Tabs dropped onto groups or beside other tabs will also use `sendToGroup`. This replaces the current `moveTab` behavior that refused dormant leaves.

A pool band will be rendered inside each section for dropping tabs. Tabs can also be dropped onto the middle of a section header to enter the pool. `canDropAt` will allow drops into sections, and `computeDropPosition` will treat the section middle as an "into" target.

Dropping a tab beside a group would insert it as a sibling of groups within the section. The pool band would then sit between groups. renderSection iterates children in order, so tabs would appear mixed with groups.

Pool tabs and groups will render in two separate blocks inside each section. Pool tabs appear first, then groups follow. This avoids interleaving them by order. Tabs dropped into a section append among all children, so their order may sit after groups.

Tab row clicks will only highlight the tab. The focusTab action is removed from the click handler. The wireRowClick delay remains.

Ctrl-click on a sidebar tab row toggles its selection. The context menu uses that selection when the row is included.

The tab menu will show a "Send to pool" submenu for sections. It will show a "Send to group" submenu for non-completed groups except the current one. It will show "Return to {origin}" if the tab has an origin. It will also keep the existing "Dock this tab" option.

Docking a group will target the pane that currently holds the open leaf. It will not dock the pool.

export type NodeType = 'section' | 'group' | 'tab';

/**
 * Colour-coding palette. Stored as a slot id, never a hex -- every slot maps to
 * a CSS custom property (see styles.css), which in turn defers to Obsidian's own
 * `--color-*` variables, so a colour picked in a dark theme stays right after
 * switching to a light one. A stored hex would be frozen to whichever theme
 * happened to be active when it was chosen.
 *
 * Order matters: it's the rotation auto-assignment walks (see
 * TabSpacesStore.pickAutoColor), so the first few slots are the ones most
 * people will actually see.
 */
export const COLOR_SLOTS = ['blue', 'purple', 'green', 'orange', 'cyan', 'pink', 'yellow', 'red'] as const;

export type ColorSlot = (typeof COLOR_SLOTS)[number];

/** What a group/section can be set to. The `'none'` sentinel is deliberately
 * distinct from leaving `color` unset: unset means "inherit" (follow my
 * section, or fall back to my auto-assigned slot), while `'none'` is an
 * explicit "show no colour at all" that a section's colour can't override. */
export type ColorChoice = ColorSlot | 'none';

export const COLOR_LABELS: Record<ColorSlot, string> = {
	blue: 'Blue',
	purple: 'Purple',
	green: 'Green',
	orange: 'Orange',
	cyan: 'Cyan',
	pink: 'Pink',
	yellow: 'Yellow',
	red: 'Red',
};

export type PaneType = 'tab' | 'split' | 'window';

export interface OpenBehavior {
	mode: PaneType;
	/** Only meaningful when mode === 'split'. */
	direction?: 'vertical' | 'horizontal';
}

/**
 * A single flat tree, same shape for sections/groups/tabs -- reorder,
 * reparent (move to another group/section), rename, and delete all become
 * one generic operation each instead of three parallel implementations.
 */
export interface SpaceNode {
	id: string;
	type: NodeType;
	title: string;
	/** null = root level. Or a real section/group id. Or one of the sentinels below. */
	parentId: string | null;
	order: number;

	/** Groups and sections only. */
	collapsed?: boolean;
	/** Groups and sections -- optional short note shown below the title. */
	description?: string;

	/** Groups only -- how this group's tabs get opened when activated. */
	openBehavior?: OpenBehavior;
	/** Groups only -- the WorkspaceTabs pane id this group claims while live. */
	homePaneId?: string;
	/** Legacy leaf-anchor claim; cleared on first reconcile after load (replaced by homePaneId). */
	homeLeafId?: string;
	/** Groups and sections. For a group: when true, its pane is hidden from
	 * the main workspace (not closed, still open in the background -- see
	 * LeafSync.applyHiddenClass). For a section: when true, every group filed
	 * under it is treated as hidden too, regardless of that group's own flag
	 * -- see LeafSync.isEffectivelyHidden. */
	hidden?: boolean;

	/** Groups and sections -- the colour the user explicitly picked. Absent
	 * means "inherit", which is the default state: a group filed under a
	 * section shows that section's colour, so dragging a group in adopts the
	 * section instantly and dragging it out returns it to its own.
	 *
	 * An explicit colour outranks inheritance but is *not* permanent: filing a
	 * group into a section clears it, so the group joins the section's colour
	 * rather than sitting inside it looking unrelated (see
	 * TabSpacesStore.moveInto). It survives reordering within a section, and
	 * survives being completed and restored.
	 *
	 * `'none'` is an explicit "no colour at all" that a section can't override.
	 * See TabSpacesStore.effectiveColor for the full resolution order. */
	color?: ColorChoice;
	/** Groups and sections -- the slot handed out automatically at creation, so
	 * colour coding works without anyone opening a menu. Only consulted once
	 * nothing above it in the chain has an explicit `color`, which is why a
	 * group's own autoColor stays dormant for as long as it lives in a
	 * section. Never shown to the user as a choice; picking any colour writes
	 * `color` instead, and "Automatic" clears that to fall back here. */
	autoColor?: ColorSlot;

	/** Tabs only -- internal matching key used by reconcile to tell "same tab, still
	 * open" apart from "closed". Equals filePath for note/file tabs (stable across
	 * restarts); for tabs with no file (a terminal, web viewer, etc.) it's a
	 * session-scoped `viewType:leafId` -- those can't be restart-matched in general,
	 * which just reflects that most non-file views aren't restorable that way either. */
	tabKey?: string;
	/** Tabs only -- set when this tab is backed by a real vault file; used to reopen
	 * it via openFile() and to survive restarts. Absent for non-file tabs (terminal,
	 * web viewer, canvas without a file, etc.) -- those rely on `viewState` alone. */
	filePath?: string;
	/** Tabs only -- raw leaf.getViewState(). For file tabs this preserves fidelity
	 * (mode/scroll); for non-file tabs it's the *only* way to reopen them at all. */
	viewState?: unknown;
	/** Tabs only -- cosmetic "done" checkbox; never closes or removes the tab. */
	done?: boolean;
	/** Tabs only -- set once the title has been explicitly renamed via this
	 * plugin's own UI, so reconcile's live-title sync (e.g. picking up a
	 * renamed Terminus tab or a browser tab's title loading in) stops
	 * overwriting it. */
	titleOverridden?: boolean;

	/** Groups only, once moved under COMPLETED_PARENT_ID. */
	completedAt?: number;
	/** Groups only -- where to restore to if its original section/parent is gone. */
	lastParentId?: string | null;

	/** Tabs only. Set when the tab is filed in a section pool, so Return can
	 * put the row back in the group it left. Cleared when Send to a group
	 * makes that group the new home. */
	originGroupId?: string;
	/** Index among the origin group's children at the time it was pooled. */
	originOrder?: number;
}

/** Reserved parentId value for the Completed bucket, so it reuses the same node
 * machinery (rename/delete/restore/drag all keep working with zero special-casing)
 * instead of living in a separate array. Never collides with a real id since
 * generateId() only ever produces base36 timestamp+random strings. */
export const COMPLETED_PARENT_ID = '__completed__';

export type TitleOverflow = 'truncate' | 'wrap';

export interface TabSpacesSettings {
	confirmBeforeComplete: boolean;
	defaultOpenBehavior: OpenBehavior;
	titleOverflow: TitleOverflow;
	/** Hides Obsidian's native tab-header row globally -- pairs with the "New tab"
	 * group-menu item, since that row is also where the native "+" button lives. */
	hideTabHeaders: boolean;
	/** Master switch for colour coding. Off suppresses every stripe and swatch
	 * without touching a single stored colour, so turning it back on restores
	 * exactly what was set before -- and it spares anyone who doesn't want the
	 * feature from setting "No colour" on every group forever, only for the
	 * next auto-assigned one to arrive coloured anyway. */
	colorCoding: boolean;
}

export interface TabSpacesData {
	items: SpaceNode[];
	settings: TabSpacesSettings;
	/** At most one section is focused; null/absent means none. */
	focusedSectionId?: string | null;
}

export const DEFAULT_SETTINGS: TabSpacesSettings = {
	confirmBeforeComplete: true,
	defaultOpenBehavior: { mode: 'tab' },
	titleOverflow: 'truncate',
	hideTabHeaders: false,
	colorCoding: true,
};

export const DEFAULT_DATA: TabSpacesData = {
	items: [],
	settings: DEFAULT_SETTINGS,
};

export const VIEW_TYPE_WORKING_TABS = 'working-tabs-view';

export function generateId(): string {
	return Date.now().toString(36) + Math.random().toString(36).substring(2, 9);
}

import type { SpaceNode } from './types';
import { COMPLETED_PARENT_ID } from './types';

/** Minimal view-state shape used by blank-tab detection -- avoids importing Obsidian. */
export type PlanViewState = { type?: string; state?: Record<string, unknown> };

export interface TabIdentity {
	key: string;
	path?: string;
	title: string;
}

export interface SnapshotLeaf {
	leafId: string;
	identity: TabIdentity;
	viewState?: PlanViewState;
}

export interface SnapshotPane {
	paneId: string;
	leaves: SnapshotLeaf[];
}

export interface WorkspaceSnapshot {
	panes: SnapshotPane[];
}

export interface PlanContext {
	mode: 'full' | 'poll';
	focusedSectionId: string | null;
	suppressedGroupIds: ReadonlySet<string>;
	nextDefaultTitle: () => string;
}

export type PlanEntry =
	| { kind: 'claimPane'; groupId: string; paneId: string }
	| { kind: 'releasePane'; groupId: string }
	| { kind: 'syncTitle'; tabId: string; title: string }
	| { kind: 'syncViewState'; tabId: string; viewState: PlanViewState }
	| { kind: 'setOrder'; tabId: string; order: number }
	| { kind: 'moveTabRecord'; tabId: string; fromGroupId: string; toGroupId: string }
	| { kind: 'addTab'; groupId: string; key: string; path?: string; title: string; viewState?: PlanViewState }
	| { kind: 'pruneTab'; tabId: string }
	| { kind: 'newGroup'; paneId: string; parentId: string | null; title: string }
	| { kind: 'merged'; fromGroup: SpaceNode; toGroupId: string; tabIds: string[] }
	| { kind: 'removeGroup'; groupId: string };

/** Provisional groupId on addTab entries that follow a newGroup for the same pane. */
export function pendingGroupId(paneId: string): string {
	return `__new__:${paneId}`;
}

/** A tab with nothing to restore -- a blank "New tab" pane. */
export function isBlankTab(tab: SpaceNode): boolean {
	if (tab.filePath) return false;
	const type = (tab.viewState as PlanViewState | undefined)?.type;
	return !type || type === 'empty';
}

/** Stored hide flags only. Focus does not hide panes — that pulled flex items out of Obsidian's split tree. */
export function effectivelyHidden(
	group: Pick<SpaceNode, 'hidden'>,
	section: Pick<SpaceNode, 'hidden'> | undefined
): boolean {
	if (group.hidden) return true;
	if (section?.hidden) return true;
	return false;
}

function childrenOf(nodes: SpaceNode[], parentId: string): SpaceNode[] {
	return nodes
		.filter((n) => n.parentId === parentId)
		.sort((a, b) => a.order - b.order);
}

/**
 * Pure membership plan: workspace snapshot + store nodes → ordered PlanEntry list.
 * No Obsidian imports; LeafSync applies the result inside one store.batch.
 */
export function plan(
	snapshot: WorkspaceSnapshot,
	nodes: SpaceNode[],
	ctx: PlanContext
): PlanEntry[] {
	const entries: PlanEntry[] = [];
	const paneById = new Map(snapshot.panes.map((p) => [p.paneId, p]));
	const paneIds = new Set(paneById.keys());

	const tabs = nodes.filter((n) => n.type === 'tab');
	const tabByKey = new Map<string, SpaceNode>();
	for (const tab of tabs) {
		if (tab.tabKey) tabByKey.set(tab.tabKey, tab);
	}

	const groups = nodes.filter((n) => n.type === 'group' && n.parentId !== COMPLETED_PARENT_ID);

	// Effective parent of each tab after moves emitted this pass (pure — no node mutation).
	const effectiveParent = new Map<string, string>();
	for (const tab of tabs) {
		if (tab.parentId) effectiveParent.set(tab.id, tab.parentId);
	}

	const claimByGroup = new Map<string, string>();
	const claimByPane = new Map<string, string>();
	for (const g of groups) {
		if (g.homePaneId && paneIds.has(g.homePaneId)) {
			claimByGroup.set(g.id, g.homePaneId);
			claimByPane.set(g.homePaneId, g.id);
		}
	}

	const movedOut = new Map<string, { toGroupId: string; tabIds: string[] }>();
	const movedTabIds = new Set<string>();

	// 1. Live sync
	for (const pane of snapshot.panes) {
		for (const leaf of pane.leaves) {
			const tab = tabByKey.get(leaf.identity.key);
			if (!tab) continue;
			entries.push({ kind: 'syncTitle', tabId: tab.id, title: leaf.identity.title });
			if (ctx.mode === 'full' && leaf.viewState) {
				entries.push({ kind: 'syncViewState', tabId: tab.id, viewState: leaf.viewState });
			}
		}
	}

	// 2. Claims — keep / release
	for (const g of groups) {
		if (!g.homePaneId) continue;
		if (paneIds.has(g.homePaneId)) {
			entries.push({ kind: 'claimPane', groupId: g.id, paneId: g.homePaneId });
		} else {

		for (const g of reattachCandidates) {
			if (claimByGroup.has(g.id)) continue;
			const nonDone = childrenOf(nodes, g.id).filter((t) => !t.done && t.tabKey);
			if (nonDone.length === 0) continue;
			if (!nonDone.every((t) => paneKeys.has(t.tabKey as string))) continue;
			entries.push({ kind: 'claimPane', groupId: g.id, paneId: pane.paneId });

		if (hosts.length !== 1) continue;

	for (const pane of snapshot.panes) {
		if (claimByPane.has(pane.paneId)) continue;
		entries.push({
			kind: 'newGroup',
			paneId: pane.paneId,

			title: ctx.nextDefaultTitle(),

		for (const leaf of pane.leaves) {
			entries.push({
				kind: 'addTab',
				groupId: gid,
				key: leaf.identity.key,
				path: leaf.identity.path,
				title: leaf.identity.title,
				viewState: leaf.viewState,
			});
		}

	| { kind: 'setOrder'; tabId: string; order: number }
	| { kind: 'moveTabRecord'; tabId: string; fromGroupId: string; toGroupId: string }
	| { kind: 'addTab'; groupId: string; key: string; path?: string; title: string; viewState?: PlanViewState }
	| { kind: 'pruneTab'; tabId: string }

export function pendingGroupId(paneId: string): string {
	return `__new__:${paneId}`;

export function isBlankTab(tab: SpaceNode): boolean {
	if (tab.filePath) return false;

	if (group.hidden) return true;
	if (section?.hidden) return true;
	return false;
}

/** A tab filed in a section pool. Its leaf may still be open; the record stays put. */
function isSectionPool(nodes: SpaceNode[], tab: SpaceNode): boolean {
	if (tab.type !== 'tab' || !tab.parentId) return false;
	return nodes.some((node) => node.id === tab.parentId && node.type === 'section');
}

function childrenOf(nodes: SpaceNode[], parentId: string): SpaceNode[] {
	return nodes
		.filter((n) => n.parentId === parentId)
		.sort((a, b) => a.order - b.order);
}

/**
 * Pure membership plan: workspace snapshot + store nodes → ordered PlanEntry list.
 * No Obsidian imports; LeafSync applies the result inside one store.batch.
 */
export function plan(
	snapshot: WorkspaceSnapshot,
	nodes: SpaceNode[],
	ctx: PlanContext
): PlanEntry[] {
	const entries: PlanEntry[] = [];
	const paneById = new Map(snapshot.panes.map((p) => [p.paneId, p]));
	const paneIds = new Set(paneById.keys());

	const tabs = nodes.filter((n) => n.type === 'tab');
	const tabByKey = new Map<string, SpaceNode>();
	for (const tab of tabs) {
		if (tab.tabKey) tabByKey.set(tab.tabKey, tab);
	}

	const groups = nodes.filter((n) => n.type === 'group' && n.parentId !== COMPLETED_PARENT_ID);

	// Effective parent of each tab after moves emitted this pass (pure — no node mutation).
	const effectiveParent = new Map<string, string>();
	for (const tab of tabs) {
		if (tab.parentId) effectiveParent.set(tab.id, tab.parentId);
	}

	const claimByGroup = new Map<string, string>();
	const claimByPane = new Map<string, string>();
	for (const g of groups) {
		if (g.homePaneId && paneIds.has(g.homePaneId)) {
			claimByGroup.set(g.id, g.homePaneId);
			claimByPane.set(g.homePaneId, g.id);
		}
	}

	const movedOut = new Map<string, { toGroupId: string; tabIds: string[] }>();
	const movedTabIds = new Set<string>();

	// 1. Live sync
	for (const pane of snapshot.panes) {
		for (const leaf of pane.leaves) {
			const tab = tabByKey.get(leaf.identity.key);
			if (!tab) continue;
			entries.push({ kind: 'syncTitle', tabId: tab.id, title: leaf.identity.title });
			if (ctx.mode === 'full' && leaf.viewState) {
				entries.push({ kind: 'syncViewState', tabId: tab.id, viewState: leaf.viewState });
			}
		}
	}

	// 2. Claims — keep / release
	for (const g of groups) {
		if (!g.homePaneId) continue;
		if (paneIds.has(g.homePaneId)) {
			entries.push({ kind: 'claimPane', groupId: g.id, paneId: g.homePaneId });
		} else {
			entries.push({ kind: 'releasePane', groupId: g.id });
			claimByGroup.delete(g.id);

			let survivors = 0;
			for (const tab of childrenOf(nodes, g.id)) {
				if (!tab.done && isBlankTab(tab)) {
					entries.push({ kind: 'pruneTab', tabId: tab.id });
				} else {
					survivors++;
				}
			}
			if (survivors === 0) {
				entries.push({ kind: 'removeGroup', groupId: g.id });
			}
		}
	}

	// 3. Reattach (D7) — every non-done tab key present in the unclaimed pane
	const reattachCandidates = groups.filter(
		(g) => !claimByGroup.has(g.id) && g.parentId !== COMPLETED_PARENT_ID
	);

	for (const pane of snapshot.panes) {
		if (claimByPane.has(pane.paneId)) continue;
		const paneKeys = new Set(pane.leaves.map((l) => l.identity.key));
		for (const g of reattachCandidates) {
			if (claimByGroup.has(g.id)) continue;
			const nonDone = childrenOf(nodes, g.id).filter((t) => !t.done && t.tabKey);
			if (nonDone.length === 0) continue;
			if (!nonDone.every((t) => paneKeys.has(t.tabKey as string))) continue;
			entries.push({ kind: 'claimPane', groupId: g.id, paneId: pane.paneId });
			claimByGroup.set(g.id, pane.paneId);
			claimByPane.set(pane.paneId, g.id);
			break;
		}
	}

	// A live group whose pane is gone, and whose non-done tabs all sit in one
	// remaining claimed pane, moves those records instead of copying them.
	// The snapshot has no empty pane, so the later merge step never sees this.
	for (const g of groups) {
		if (claimByGroup.has(g.id) || !g.homePaneId) continue;
		const nonDone = childrenOf(nodes, g.id).filter((t) => !t.done && t.tabKey);
		if (nonDone.length === 0) continue;
		const hosts = snapshot.panes.filter((pane) => {
			const keys = new Set(pane.leaves.map((l) => l.identity.key));
			return nonDone.every((t) => keys.has(t.tabKey as string));
		});
		if (hosts.length !== 1) continue;
		const hostId = claimByPane.get(hosts[0].paneId);
		if (!hostId || hostId === g.id) continue;
		const tabIds: string[] = [];
		for (const tab of nonDone) {
			entries.push({
				kind: 'moveTabRecord',
				tabId: tab.id,
				fromGroupId: g.id,
				toGroupId: hostId,
			});
			movedTabIds.add(tab.id);
			effectiveParent.set(tab.id, hostId);
			tabIds.push(tab.id);
		}
		entries.push({
			kind: 'merged',
			fromGroup: { ...g },
			toGroupId: hostId,
			tabIds,
		});
		entries.push({ kind: 'removeGroup', groupId: g.id });
	}

	// 4. Mirror (D1) — moves/adds for every claimed pane first, then prunes/order.
	// Two passes so a swap between live panes never prune+adds the same key.
	const mirrorTargets: Array<{ paneId: string; groupId: string }> = [];
	for (const [paneId, groupId] of claimByPane) {
		if (ctx.suppressedGroupIds.has(groupId)) continue;
		mirrorTargets.push({ paneId, groupId });
	}

	for (const { paneId, groupId } of mirrorTargets) {
		const pane = paneById.get(paneId);
		if (!pane) continue;

		for (const leaf of pane.leaves) {
			const key = leaf.identity.key;
			const existing = tabByKey.get(key);
			if (!existing) {
				entries.push({
					kind: 'addTab',
					groupId,
					key,
					path: leaf.identity.path,
					title: leaf.identity.title,
					viewState: leaf.viewState,
				});
				continue;
			}

			if (isSectionPool(nodes, existing)) continue;

			const fromId = effectiveParent.get(existing.id);
			if (fromId === groupId) continue;

			const fromGroup = fromId ? groups.find((n) => n.id === fromId) : undefined;
			const fromIsLive = Boolean(fromGroup && claimByGroup.has(fromGroup.id));

			if (fromIsLive && fromGroup) {
				entries.push({
					kind: 'moveTabRecord',
					tabId: existing.id,
					fromGroupId: fromGroup.id,
					toGroupId: groupId,
				});
				movedTabIds.add(existing.id);
				effectiveParent.set(existing.id, groupId);

				const bucket = movedOut.get(fromGroup.id) ?? { toGroupId: groupId, tabIds: [] };
				if (bucket.tabIds.length > 0 && bucket.toGroupId !== groupId) {
					bucket.toGroupId = '';
				} else {
					bucket.toGroupId = groupId;
				}
				bucket.tabIds.push(existing.id);
				movedOut.set(fromGroup.id, bucket);
			} else {
				// Dormant (or unknown) source — leave that list alone; add here.
				entries.push({
					kind: 'addTab',
					groupId,
					key,
					path: leaf.identity.path,
					title: leaf.identity.title,
					viewState: leaf.viewState,
				});
			}
		}
	}

	for (const { paneId, groupId } of mirrorTargets) {
		const pane = paneById.get(paneId);
		if (!pane) continue;
		const paneKeys = pane.leaves.map((l) => l.identity.key);
		const paneKeySet = new Set(paneKeys);

		for (const tab of childrenOf(nodes, groupId)) {
			if (tab.done) continue;
			if (effectiveParent.get(tab.id) !== groupId) continue;
			if (movedTabIds.has(tab.id)) continue;
			if (!tab.tabKey || !paneKeySet.has(tab.tabKey)) {
				entries.push({ kind: 'pruneTab', tabId: tab.id });
			}
		}

		const liveTabs: SpaceNode[] = [];
		const seen = new Set<string>();
		for (const key of paneKeys) {
			const tab = tabByKey.get(key);
			if (!tab || seen.has(tab.id)) continue;
			if (effectiveParent.get(tab.id) !== groupId) continue;
			liveTabs.push(tab);
			seen.add(tab.id);
		}
		const rest = childrenOf(nodes, groupId).filter(
			(t) => effectiveParent.get(t.id) === groupId && !seen.has(t.id)
		);
		let order = 0;
		for (const tab of [...liveTabs, ...rest]) {
			entries.push({ kind: 'setOrder', tabId: tab.id, order: order++ });
		}
	}

	// 5. Merge detection (D3) — H ends with zero non-done tabs, all moved to a single G
	for (const g of groups) {
		if (!claimByGroup.has(g.id) && !g.homePaneId) continue;
		const move = movedOut.get(g.id);
		if (!move || !move.toGroupId || move.tabIds.length === 0) continue;

		const nonDoneRemaining = tabs.filter(
			(t) => !t.done && effectiveParent.get(t.id) === g.id
		);
		if (nonDoneRemaining.length > 0) continue;

		const paneId = claimByGroup.get(g.id);
		if (paneId) {
			entries.push({ kind: 'releasePane', groupId: g.id });
			claimByGroup.delete(g.id);
			claimByPane.delete(paneId);
		}
		entries.push({
			kind: 'merged',
			fromGroup: { ...g },
			toGroupId: move.toGroupId,
			tabIds: [...move.tabIds],
		});
		entries.push({ kind: 'removeGroup', groupId: g.id });
	}

	// 6. New groups for still-unclaimed panes.
	// A leaf whose record sits in a section pool stays that record. It does not
	// spawn another tab, and a pane of only pooled leaves does not spawn a group.
	for (const pane of snapshot.panes) {
		if (claimByPane.has(pane.paneId)) continue;
		const freshLeaves = pane.leaves.filter((leaf) => {
			const existing = tabByKey.get(leaf.identity.key);
			return !(existing && isSectionPool(nodes, existing));
		});
		if (freshLeaves.length === 0) continue;
		entries.push({
			kind: 'newGroup',
			paneId: pane.paneId,
			parentId: null,
			title: ctx.nextDefaultTitle(),
		});
		const gid = pendingGroupId(pane.paneId);
		for (const leaf of freshLeaves) {
			entries.push({
				kind: 'addTab',
				groupId: gid,
				key: leaf.identity.key,
				path: leaf.identity.path,
				title: leaf.identity.title,
				viewState: leaf.viewState,
			});
		}
		claimByPane.set(pane.paneId, gid);
	}

	return entries;
}

import type TabSpacesPlugin from './main';
import {
	type SpaceNode,
	type TabSpacesData,
	type TabSpacesSettings,
	type OpenBehavior,
	type ColorSlot,
	type ColorChoice,
	COLOR_SLOTS,
	DEFAULT_DATA,
	DEFAULT_SETTINGS,
	COMPLETED_PARENT_ID,
	generateId,
} from './types';

/** Retired sentinel: groups used to get parked here until organized. Now
 * every detected pane is a real, permanent, root-level group from the
 * moment it's created, so this bucket no longer exists -- only kept here to
 * migrate anything still pointing at it from before the change. */
const LEGACY_UNSORTED_PARENT_ID = '__unsorted__';

export class TabSpacesStore {
	private plugin: TabSpacesPlugin;
	private data: TabSpacesData;
	private listeners: Array<() => void> = [];

	constructor(plugin: TabSpacesPlugin) {
		this.plugin = plugin;
		this.data = { items: [], settings: { ...DEFAULT_SETTINGS } };
	}

	async load(): Promise<void> {
		const saved = (await this.plugin.loadData()) as Partial<TabSpacesData> | null;
		this.data = {
			items: saved?.items ?? DEFAULT_DATA.items,
			settings: { ...DEFAULT_SETTINGS, ...(saved?.settings ?? {}) },
			focusedSectionId: saved?.focusedSectionId ?? null,
		};
		// One-time migration: anything still filed under the retired Unsorted
		// bucket becomes a normal root-level group/tab, same as everything else.
		for (const item of this.data.items) {
			if (item.parentId === LEGACY_UNSORTED_PARENT_ID) item.parentId = null;
		}
		// Colour coding arrived after these groups/sections were created, so
		// backfill the slot they'd have been handed at creation -- otherwise
		// existing users would see an uncoloured sidebar until they made
		// something new, which reads as the feature being broken.
		for (const item of this.data.items) {
			if ((item.type === 'group' || item.type === 'section') && !item.autoColor) {
				item.autoColor = this.pickAutoColor();
			}
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Hands out the least-used slot, so a handful of groups and sections come
	 * out visibly different instead of the rotation doubling back early.
	 *
	 * Groups and sections share one rotation rather than counting separately:
	 * a section's stripe and a root-level group's stripe show up side by side
	 * in the same workspace, so letting each type restart the rotation would
	 * reliably hand the first section the same colour as the first group --
	 * exactly the collision the feature exists to prevent.
	 *
	 * Counts `autoColor` only: an explicit user choice shouldn't push the
	 * automatic rotation around.
	 */
	private pickAutoColor(): ColorSlot {
		const used = new Map<ColorSlot, number>(COLOR_SLOTS.map((slot) => [slot, 0]));
		for (const node of this.data.items) {
			if (!node.autoColor) continue;
			used.set(node.autoColor, (used.get(node.autoColor) ?? 0) + 1);
		}
		let best: ColorSlot = COLOR_SLOTS[0];
		for (const slot of COLOR_SLOTS) {
			if ((used.get(slot) ?? 0) < (used.get(best) ?? 0)) best = slot;
		}
		return best;
	}

	/**
	 * The colour a group/section actually displays, resolved in this order:
	 * the node's own explicit pick, then whatever its section resolves to
	 * (recursively, so a section nested in a section still follows), then its
	 * own auto-assigned slot.
	 *
	 * Inheritance living here -- rather than being copied onto each group when
	 * it's filed -- is what makes drag-into-a-section adopt the section colour
	 * with no move-time bookkeeping at all, and drag-back-out restore the
	 * group's own. Nothing has to notice the move; the answer is just derived
	 * fresh each time it's asked for.
	 */
	effectiveColor(node: SpaceNode): ColorSlot | undefined {
		// The single choke point every stripe and swatch already runs through,
		// which is what lets the master switch be one line instead of a
		// suppression rule duplicated across the sidebar and the workspace.
		if (!this.data.settings.colorCoding) return undefined;
		if (node.type !== 'group' && node.type !== 'section') return undefined;
		if (node.color) return node.color === 'none' ? undefined : node.color;
		const parent = node.parentId ? this.find(node.parentId) : undefined;
		// A section set to 'none' hands back undefined here, so its groups go
		// uncoloured with it -- no separate rule needed for the section case.
		if (parent?.type === 'section') return this.effectiveColor(parent);
		return node.autoColor;
	}

	/** `color: undefined` is "Automatic" -- back to inheriting from the section
	 * (or to this node's own auto-assigned slot when it isn't in one).
	 * `'none'` is the explicit opt-out, which inheritance can't override. */
	async setColor(id: string, color: ColorChoice | undefined): Promise<void> {
		const node = this.find(id);
		if (!node || (node.type !== 'group' && node.type !== 'section')) return;
		node.color = color;
		await this.save();
		this.notify();
	}

	/** Drops every explicit colour inside a section, so groups that had been
	 * individually recoloured fall back to following the section again. The
	 * "make this whole section one colour" escape hatch, kept as its own
	 * deliberate action rather than a side effect of setting the section's
	 * colour -- which would silently discard per-group choices. */
	async clearChildColors(sectionId: string): Promise<void> {
		let changed = false;
		for (const child of this.children(sectionId)) {
			if (child.color === undefined) continue;
			child.color = undefined;
			changed = true;
		}
		if (!changed) return;
		await this.save();
		this.notify();

	/**
	 * Collapses every mutation made inside `fn` into a single disk write and a
	 * single change notification.
	 *
	 * Each mutator below ends in `save(); notify()`, which is right for a lone
	 * user action but pathological for a reconcile pass: that walks every open
	 * tab and can call syncTitle/syncViewState/setOrder on each, so an N-tab
	 * workspace paid N full `saveData()` serializations of the entire store
	 * plus N full sidebar re-renders -- all synchronous, all on the same main
	 * thread that xterm.js needs to accept keystrokes and paint. Batching turns
	 * that back into one of each.
	 *
	 * Re-entrant (depth-counted) because reconcile's helpers call each other,
	 * and flushed in a `finally` so a throw mid-pass still persists whatever
	 * already changed rather than silently dropping it.
	 */
	async batch<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
		this.batchDepth++;
		try {
			return await fn();
		} finally {
			this.batchDepth--;
			if (this.batchDepth === 0 && this.batchPending) {
				this.batchPending = false;
				await this.plugin.saveData(this.data);
				this.notify();
			}
		}
	}

	private batchDepth = 0;
	private batchPending = false;

	async save(): Promise<void> {
		if (this.batchDepth > 0) {
			this.batchPending = true;
			return;
		}
		await this.plugin.saveData(this.data);
	}

	onChange(listener: () => void): () => void {
		this.listeners.push(listener);
		return () => {
			this.listeners = this.listeners.filter((l) => l !== listener);
		};
	}

	private notify(): void {
		if (this.batchDepth > 0) {
			this.batchPending = true;
			return;
		}
		for (const listener of this.listeners) listener();
	}

	get settings(): TabSpacesSettings {
		return this.data.settings;
	}

	async updateSettings(patch: Partial<TabSpacesSettings>): Promise<void> {
		this.data.settings = { ...this.data.settings, ...patch };
		await this.save();
		this.notify();
	}

	get items(): SpaceNode[] {
		return this.data.items;
	}

	find(id: string): SpaceNode | undefined {
		return this.data.items.find((i) => i.id === id);
	}

	children(parentId: string | null): SpaceNode[] {
		return this.data.items
			.filter((item) => item.parentId === parentId)
			.sort((a, b) => a.order - b.order);
	}

	private nextOrder(parentId: string | null): number {
		const siblings = this.children(parentId);
		return siblings.length > 0 ? Math.max(...siblings.map((s) => s.order)) + 1 : 0;
	}

	/** Default title for a freshly-created group/section -- "Group 1",
	 * "Section 1", etc. -- since neither is named up front (a group is
	 * auto-created the moment a pane appears; a section is created instantly
	 * with no naming prompt). Renaming later is just the normal rename flow. */
	nextDefaultTitle(type: 'group' | 'section'): string {
		const count = this.data.items.filter((n) => n.type === type).length;
		const label = type === 'group' ? 'Group' : 'Section';
		return `${label} ${count + 1}`;
	}

	async addSection(title: string, parentId: string | null = null): Promise<SpaceNode> {
		const node: SpaceNode = {
			id: generateId(),
			type: 'section',
			title,
			parentId,
			order: this.nextOrder(parentId),
			collapsed: false,
			autoColor: this.pickAutoColor(),
		};
		this.data.items.push(node);
		await this.save();
		this.notify();
		return node;
	}

	async addGroup(
		title: string,
		parentId: string | null = null,
		openBehavior: OpenBehavior = this.data.settings.defaultOpenBehavior
	): Promise<SpaceNode> {
		const node: SpaceNode = {
			id: generateId(),
			type: 'group',
			title,
			parentId,
			order: this.nextOrder(parentId),
			collapsed: false,
			openBehavior: { ...openBehavior },
			autoColor: this.pickAutoColor(),
		};
		this.data.items.push(node);
		await this.save();
		this.notify();
		return node;
	}

	/** Re-inserts a group node (e.g. merge undo) with its existing id. */
	async insertGroup(node: SpaceNode): Promise<void> {
		if (node.type !== 'group' || this.find(node.id)) return;
		const parentId = node.parentId && this.find(node.parentId) ? node.parentId : null;
		node.parentId = parentId;
		node.homePaneId = undefined;
		node.homeLeafId = undefined;
		node.order = this.nextOrder(parentId);
		this.data.items.push(node);
		await this.save();
		this.notify();
	}

	async addTab(
		groupId: string,
		tabKey: string,
		title: string,
		options: { filePath?: string; viewState?: unknown } = {}
	): Promise<SpaceNode> {
		const node: SpaceNode = {
			id: generateId(),
			type: 'tab',
			title,
			parentId: groupId,
			order: this.nextOrder(groupId),
			tabKey,
			filePath: options.filePath,
			viewState: options.viewState,
		};
		this.data.items.push(node);
		await this.save();
		this.notify();
		return node;
	}

	/** The user-facing rename (dblclick, F2, "Rename" menu item). Marks a tab's
	 * title as overridden so reconcile's live-title sync (see syncTitle) never
	 * clobbers a name the user deliberately chose. */
	async rename(id: string, title: string): Promise<void> {
		const node = this.find(id);
		if (!node) return;
		node.title = title;
		if (node.type === 'tab') node.titleOverridden = true;
		await this.save();
		this.notify();
	}

	/** Reconcile-only: keeps a tab's title in step with its live view (a
	 * renamed Terminus tab, a browser tab's title loading in, etc.), unless
	 * the user has explicitly renamed it via `rename()` above. */
	async syncTitle(id: string, title: string): Promise<void> {
		const node = this.find(id);
		if (!node || node.type !== 'tab' || node.titleOverridden || node.title === title) return;
		node.title = title;
		await this.save();
		this.notify();
	}

	/** Reconcile-only: keeps a tab's full view state in step with its live
	 * view. Titles get their own explicit sync (with an override guard) since
	 * users can rename those; there's no equivalent user-facing edit for view
	 * state, so it's always kept fresh -- this is the only place a URL lives
	 * for a browser tab, so without it, navigating within an already-tracked
	 * tab would silently go stale and reopening it later would land back on
	 * whatever page was open when it was first captured, not wherever it
	 * actually ended up. JSON-compares before writing so an unchanged tab
	 * (the common case on most reconcile passes) doesn't touch disk. */
	async syncViewState(id: string, viewState: unknown): Promise<void> {
		const node = this.find(id);
		if (!node || node.type !== 'tab') return;
		const next = JSON.stringify(viewState);
		if (JSON.stringify(node.viewState) === next) return;
		node.viewState = viewState;
		await this.save();
		this.notify();
	}

	/** Follows a vault file rename into every tab tracking it (`filePath` and
	 * `tabKey` are the same string for file-backed tabs) -- without this, a
	 * renamed file's old path stops matching anything open, so the tab looks
	 * closed to reconcile and either gets knocked out of its group as a
	 * "new" ad hoc one, or, if marked done, is left permanently pointing at a
	 * path that no longer exists. */
	async remapTabPath(oldPath: string, newPath: string, newTitle: string): Promise<void> {
		let changed = false;
		for (const node of this.data.items) {
			if (node.type !== 'tab' || node.filePath !== oldPath) continue;
			node.filePath = newPath;
			node.tabKey = newPath;
			if (!node.titleOverridden) node.title = newTitle;
			const state = (node.viewState as { state?: Record<string, unknown> } | undefined)?.state;
			if (state && state.file === oldPath) state.file = newPath;
			changed = true;
		}
		if (!changed) return;
		await this.save();
		this.notify();
	}

	/** Reconcile-only: re-derives a tab's stored order from its live tab-strip
	 * position, so dragging the actual Obsidian tabs updates the sidebar too.
	 * No-ops if the order already matches, so a normal reconcile pass with
	 * nothing to fix doesn't write to disk. */
	async setOrder(id: string, order: number): Promise<void> {
		const node = this.find(id);
		if (!node || node.order === order) return;
		node.order = order;
		await this.save();
		this.notify();
	}

	async toggleCollapsed(id: string): Promise<void> {
		const node = this.find(id);
		if (!node || (node.type !== 'group' && node.type !== 'section')) return;
		node.collapsed = !node.collapsed;
		await this.save();
		this.notify();
	}

	/** Purely cosmetic -- never closes or removes the tab. */
	async toggleDone(id: string): Promise<void> {
		const node = this.find(id);
		if (!node || node.type !== 'tab') return;
		node.done = !node.done;
		await this.save();
		this.notify();
	}

	async setDescription(id: string, description: string | undefined): Promise<void> {
		const node = this.find(id);
		if (!node || (node.type !== 'group' && node.type !== 'section')) return;
		node.description = description;
		await this.save();
		this.notify();
	}

	async setOpenBehavior(id: string, openBehavior: OpenBehavior): Promise<void> {
		const node = this.find(id);
		if (!node || node.type !== 'group') return;
		node.openBehavior = { ...openBehavior };
		await this.save();
		this.notify();
	}

	/** Tracks the pane a group currently claims; cleared once the pane closes. */
	async setHomePane(id: string, paneId: string | undefined): Promise<void> {
		const node = this.find(id);
		if (!node || node.type !== 'group') return;
		// Reconcile re-asserts claims every pass -- no-op when nothing changed so
		// we don't notify (and re-render the sidebar) on a quiet poll tick.
		if (node.homePaneId === paneId && !node.homeLeafId) return;
		node.homePaneId = paneId;
		node.homeLeafId = undefined;
		await this.save();
		this.notify();
	}

	/** Files a tab under a section pool. The first park remembers the group it left. */
	async parkInPool(tabId: string, sectionId: string): Promise<void> {
		const tab = this.find(tabId);
		const section = this.find(sectionId);
		if (!tab || tab.type !== 'tab' || !section || section.type !== 'section') return;
		if (!tab.originGroupId) {
			const parent = tab.parentId ? this.find(tab.parentId) : undefined;
			if (parent?.type === 'group') {
				tab.originGroupId = parent.id;
				tab.originOrder = this.children(parent.id).findIndex((child) => child.id === tab.id);
			}
		}
		const index = this.children(sectionId).filter((child) => child.id !== tab.id).length;
		await this.moveInto(tab.id, sectionId, index);
	}

	/** Puts a pooled tab back in the group it left. The group has to still exist. */
	async restoreOrigin(tabId: string): Promise<boolean> {
		const tab = this.find(tabId);
		if (!tab || tab.type !== 'tab' || !tab.originGroupId) return false;
		const group = this.find(tab.originGroupId);
		if (!group || group.type !== 'group') return false;
		const index = tab.originOrder ?? this.children(group.id).length;
		tab.originGroupId = undefined;
		tab.originOrder = undefined;
		await this.moveInto(tab.id, group.id, index);
		return true;
	}

	/** Send to a named group makes that group the home, so Return no longer applies. */
	async clearOrigin(tabId: string): Promise<void> {
		const tab = this.find(tabId);
		if (!tab || tab.type !== 'tab') return;
		if (tab.originGroupId === undefined && tab.originOrder === undefined) return;
		tab.originGroupId = undefined;
		tab.originOrder = undefined;
		await this.save();
		this.notify();
	}

	/** Reparents a tab into another group, preserving id and all tab fields. */
	async moveTabRecord(tabId: string, toGroupId: string): Promise<void> {
		const tab = this.find(tabId);
		if (!tab || tab.type !== 'tab') return;
		const target = this.find(toGroupId);
		if (!target || target.type !== 'group') return;
		if (tab.parentId === toGroupId) return;
		tab.parentId = toGroupId;
		tab.order = this.nextOrder(toGroupId);
		await this.save();
		this.notify();
	}

	get focusedSectionId(): string | null {
		return this.data.focusedSectionId ?? null;
	}

	async setFocusedSection(id: string | null): Promise<void> {
		if (this.data.focusedSectionId === id) return;
		this.data.focusedSectionId = id;
		await this.save();
		this.notify();
	}

	async toggleHidden(id: string): Promise<void> {
		const node = this.find(id);
		if (!node || (node.type !== 'group' && node.type !== 'section')) return;
		node.hidden = !node.hidden;
		await this.save();
		this.notify();
	}

	/** Removes a node. If it's a group/section, its descendants are removed too. */
	async remove(id: string): Promise<void> {
		const idsToRemove = new Set<string>([id]);
		let grew = true;
		while (grew) {
			grew = false;
			for (const item of this.data.items) {
				if (item.parentId && idsToRemove.has(item.parentId) && !idsToRemove.has(item.id)) {
					idsToRemove.add(item.id);
					grew = true;
				}
			}
		}
		this.data.items = this.data.items.filter((i) => !idsToRemove.has(i.id));
		await this.save();
		this.notify();
	}

	/** Returns true if `ancestorId` is `id` itself or one of its ancestors. */
	private isDescendantOf(id: string, ancestorId: string): boolean {
		let current = this.find(id);
		while (current) {
			if (current.id === ancestorId) return true;
			current = current.parentId ? this.find(current.parentId) : undefined;
		}
		return false;
	}

	/**
	 * Moves `id` to be a child of `newParentId`, inserted at `index` among its
	 * new siblings. Reordering within the same parent, moving a tab to a
	 * different group, and moving a group into/out of a section are all just
	 * this one operation -- no special-casing needed.
	 */
	async moveInto(
		id: string,
		newParentId: string | null,
		index: number,
		options: { adoptSectionColor?: boolean } = {}
	): Promise<void> {
		const node = this.find(id);
		if (!node) return;
		// A group/section can't be dropped into itself or one of its own descendants.
		if (newParentId && (newParentId === id || this.isDescendantOf(newParentId, id))) return;

		const previousParentId = node.parentId;
		const newParent = newParentId ? this.find(newParentId) : undefined;
		node.parentId = newParentId;

		// Filing a group into a section adopts that section's colour, even if
		// the group had one of its own: dropping something into a colour-coded
		// section is a statement about where it now belongs, and a group that
		// kept its old colour would sit in the section looking like it wasn't
		// really part of it. Clearing the override (rather than overwriting it
		// with the section's slot) is what keeps the group tracking the section
		// afterwards, including if the section is later recoloured.
		//
		// Guarded on the parent actually changing, so reordering a group *within*
		// a section doesn't wipe a colour deliberately set while it lived there.
		// Restore opts out entirely -- putting a completed group back where it
		// came from should return it as it was, not repaint it.
		if (
			(options.adoptSectionColor ?? true) &&
			node.type === 'group' &&
			node.color !== undefined &&
			newParentId !== previousParentId &&
			newParent?.type === 'section'
		) {
			node.color = undefined;
		}

		const siblings = this.children(newParentId).filter((s) => s.id !== id);
		siblings.splice(Math.max(0, Math.min(index, siblings.length)), 0, node);
		siblings.forEach((s, i) => {
			s.order = i;
		});
		await this.save();
		this.notify();
	}

	/**
	 * Marks a group done: remembers where it lived (so Restore can put it
	 * back), moves it under the reserved COMPLETED_PARENT_ID bucket. Does not
	 * touch any live leaves -- callers (leaf-sync) detach those first.
	 */
	async complete(id: string): Promise<void> {
		const node = this.find(id);
		if (!node || node.type !== 'group') return;
		node.lastParentId = node.parentId;
		node.homePaneId = undefined;
		node.homeLeafId = undefined;
		node.completedAt = Date.now();
		await this.moveInto(id, COMPLETED_PARENT_ID, this.children(COMPLETED_PARENT_ID).length);
	}

	/** Restores a completed group to its original section, or root if that's gone. */
	async restore(id: string): Promise<void> {
		const node = this.find(id);
		if (!node || node.type !== 'group') return;
		const target = node.lastParentId && this.find(node.lastParentId) ? node.lastParentId : null;
		node.completedAt = undefined;
		// Restoring is "put it back how it was", so it's the one move that
		// doesn't repaint the group to match the section it lands in.
		await this.moveInto(id, target, this.children(target).length, { adoptSectionColor: false });
	}
}

import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import type { SpaceNode } from './types';
import {
	effectivelyHidden,
	pendingGroupId,
	plan,
	type PlanContext,
	type PlanEntry,
	type WorkspaceSnapshot,
} from './membership';

function tab(
	id: string,
	parentId: string,
	key: string,
	opts: Partial<SpaceNode> = {}
): SpaceNode {
	return {
		id,
		type: 'tab',
		title: opts.title ?? key,
		parentId,
		order: opts.order ?? 0,
		tabKey: key,
		filePath: opts.filePath ?? (key.includes(':') ? undefined : key),
		viewState: opts.viewState,
		done: opts.done,
		titleOverridden: opts.titleOverridden,
	};
}

function group(id: string, opts: Partial<SpaceNode> = {}): SpaceNode {
	return {
		id,
		type: 'group',
		title: opts.title ?? id,
		parentId: opts.parentId ?? null,
		order: opts.order ?? 0,
		homePaneId: opts.homePaneId,
		hidden: opts.hidden,
	};
}

function section(id: string): SpaceNode {
	return { id, type: 'section', title: id, parentId: null, order: 0 };
}

function snap(panes: WorkspaceSnapshot['panes']): WorkspaceSnapshot {
	return { panes };
}

function pane(
	paneId: string,
	leaves: Array<{ key: string; title?: string; path?: string; viewState?: { type?: string } }>
) {
	return {
		paneId,
		leaves: leaves.map((l, i) => ({
			leafId: `${paneId}-leaf-${i}`,
			identity: {
				key: l.key,
				path: l.path ?? (l.key.includes(':') ? undefined : l.key),
				title: l.title ?? l.key,
			},
			viewState: l.viewState,
		})),
	};
}

function ctx(partial: Partial<PlanContext> = {}): PlanContext {
	let n = 0;
	return {
		mode: 'full',
		focusedSectionId: null,
		suppressedGroupIds: new Set(),
		nextDefaultTitle: () => `Group ${++n}`,
		...partial,
	};
}

function kinds(entries: PlanEntry[]): string[] {
	return entries.map((e) => e.kind);
}

function ofKind<K extends PlanEntry['kind']>(entries: PlanEntry[], kind: K): Extract<PlanEntry, { kind: K }>[] {
	return entries.filter((e): e is Extract<PlanEntry, { kind: K }> => e.kind === kind);
}

describe('plan()', () => {
	it('reattaches a dormant group when every non-done tab is in an unclaimed pane', () => {
		const nodes = [
			group('g1'),
			tab('t1', 'g1', 'a.md', { order: 0 }),
			tab('t2', 'g1', 'b.md', { order: 1 }),
		];
		const entries = plan(snap([pane('p1', [{ key: 'a.md' }, { key: 'b.md' }])]), nodes, ctx());
		expect(ofKind(entries, 'claimPane')).toEqual([{ kind: 'claimPane', groupId: 'g1', paneId: 'p1' }]);
		expect(ofKind(entries, 'newGroup')).toHaveLength(0);
	});

	it('leaves dormant intact and creates a new group on partial reattach', () => {
		const nodes = [
			group('g1'),
			tab('t1', 'g1', 'a.md', { order: 0 }),
			tab('t2', 'g1', 'b.md', { order: 1 }),
		];
		const entries = plan(snap([pane('p1', [{ key: 'a.md' }])]), nodes, ctx());
		expect(ofKind(entries, 'claimPane').filter((e) => e.groupId === 'g1')).toHaveLength(0);
		expect(ofKind(entries, 'newGroup')).toEqual([
			{ kind: 'newGroup', paneId: 'p1', parentId: null, title: 'Group 1' },
		]);
		expect(ofKind(entries, 'addTab').some((e) => e.groupId === pendingGroupId('p1') && e.key === 'a.md')).toBe(
			true
		);
		// Dormant list never mutated
		expect(ofKind(entries, 'moveTabRecord')).toHaveLength(0);
		expect(ofKind(entries, 'pruneTab').filter((e) => e.tabId === 't1' || e.tabId === 't2')).toHaveLength(0);
	});

	it('moves a tab record between live groups without destroy/recreate; done sibling not pruned', () => {
		const nodes = [
			group('gA', { homePaneId: 'pA' }),

	it('emits merged + removeGroup when every non-done tab of H moves to G', () => {

		expect(kinds(entries).includes('removeGroup')).toBe(true);
	});

	it('releases a group when its pane disappears and keeps non-blank tab list', () => {
		const nodes = [
			group('g1', { homePaneId: 'pGone' }),
			tab('t1', 'g1', 'a.md', { order: 0 }),
			tab('tBlank', 'g1', 'empty:1', {
				order: 1,
				filePath: undefined,
				viewState: { type: 'empty' },
			}),
		];
		const entries = plan(snap([]), nodes, ctx());
		expect(ofKind(entries, 'releasePane')).toEqual([{ kind: 'releasePane', groupId: 'g1' }]);
		expect(ofKind(entries, 'pruneTab').some((e) => e.tabId === 'tBlank')).toBe(true);
		expect(ofKind(entries, 'pruneTab').some((e) => e.tabId === 't1')).toBe(false);
		expect(ofKind(entries, 'removeGroup')).toHaveLength(0);
	});

	it('removes a released group that only had blank tabs', () => {
		const nodes = [
			group('g1', { homePaneId: 'pGone' }),
			tab('tBlank', 'g1', 'empty:1', {
				order: 0,
				filePath: undefined,
				viewState: { type: 'empty' },
			}),
		];
		const entries = plan(snap([]), nodes, ctx());
		expect(ofKind(entries, 'removeGroup')).toEqual([{ kind: 'removeGroup', groupId: 'g1' }]);
	});

	it('skips mirror for suppressed groups', () => {
		const nodes = [
			group('g1', { homePaneId: 'p1' }),
			tab('t1', 'g1', 'a.md', { order: 0 }),
		];
		const entries = plan(
			snap([pane('p1', [{ key: 'a.md' }, { key: 'b.md' }])]),
			nodes,
			ctx({ suppressedGroupIds: new Set(['g1']) })
		);
		expect(ofKind(entries, 'addTab')).toHaveLength(0);
		expect(ofKind(entries, 'pruneTab')).toHaveLength(0);
		expect(ofKind(entries, 'claimPane')).toEqual([{ kind: 'claimPane', groupId: 'g1', paneId: 'p1' }]);
	});

	it('files a new pane at the root even when a section is focused', () => {
		const nodes = [section('sec1')];
		const entries = plan(
			snap([pane('p1', [{ key: 'a.md' }])]),
			nodes,
			ctx({ focusedSectionId: 'sec1' })
		);
		expect(ofKind(entries, 'newGroup')).toEqual([
			{ kind: 'newGroup', paneId: 'p1', parentId: null, title: 'Group 1' },
		]);
	});

	it('moves records when a live pane vanishes and its tabs are all in one other pane', () => {
		const nodes = [
			group('H', { homePaneId: 'pGone', title: 'Source' }),
			group('G', { homePaneId: 'pG', title: 'Target' }),
			tab('t1', 'H', 'x.md', { order: 0 }),
			tab('t2', 'H', 'y.md', { order: 1 }),
			tab('t3', 'G', 'z.md', { order: 0 }),
		];
		const entries = plan(snap([pane('pG', [{ key: 'z.md' }, { key: 'x.md' }, { key: 'y.md' }])]), nodes, ctx());
		expect(ofKind(entries, 'moveTabRecord').map((e) => e.tabId).sort()).toEqual(['t1', 't2']);
		expect(ofKind(entries, 'addTab').some((e) => e.key === 'x.md' || e.key === 'y.md')).toBe(false);
