.working-tabs-title {
	/* Shrinks (and ellipsizes) under space pressure, but doesn't grow to fill
	   unused space -- so a count badge placed right after it sits snug next
	   to the text instead of being pushed to the far edge of the row. */
	flex: 0 1 auto;
	min-width: 0;
	color: var(--text-normal);
	font-size: 13px;
	font-weight: 500;
	white-space: nowrap;
	overflow: hidden;
	text-overflow: ellipsis;
}

.working-tabs-tab-row .working-tabs-title {
	font-weight: 400;
}

/* "Wrap to multiple lines" setting -- overrides the ellipsis/nowrap default above.
   Descriptions wrap alongside titles (see rule further down) so a row's two
   lines of text stay consistent. */
.working-tabs-wrap-titles .working-tabs-title {
	white-space: normal;
	overflow: visible;
	text-overflow: clip;
	word-break: break-word;
}

.working-tabs-wrap-titles .working-tabs-title-row {
	align-items: flex-start;
}

.working-tabs-title.is-done {
	color: var(--text-faint);
	text-decoration: line-through;
}

.working-tabs-section-header .working-tabs-title,
.working-tabs-synthetic-title {
	font-size: 12px;
	font-weight: 600;
}

/* A section is a folder of sessions, not another coloured group. Its chrome
   stays on Obsidian's own surfaces so it never shares a slot with a group. */
.working-tabs-cluster.is-sections .working-tabs-section:not(.working-tabs-synthetic-section) {
	background-color: var(--background-primary);
	border: 1px solid var(--background-modifier-border);
	border-radius: 8px;
	padding: 4px;
	margin-top: 8px;
}

.working-tabs-cluster.is-sections .working-tabs-colored::before {
	content: none;
}

.working-tabs-cluster.is-sections .working-tabs-group-header,
.working-tabs-cluster.is-sections .working-tabs-group-header.working-tabs-colored {
	background-color: var(--background-secondary);
}

.working-tabs-cluster.is-sections .working-tabs-group-header:hover,
.working-tabs-cluster.is-sections .working-tabs-group-header.working-tabs-colored:hover,
.working-tabs-cluster.is-sections .working-tabs-section-header:hover {
	background-color: var(--background-modifier-hover);
}

.working-tabs-cluster.is-sections .working-tabs-tab-row.working-tabs-colored,
.working-tabs-cluster.is-sections .working-tabs-tab-row.working-tabs-colored:hover {
	background-color: transparent;
}

.working-tabs-cluster.is-sections .working-tabs-section-header {
	background-color: transparent;
}

.working-tabs-text-col {
	flex: 1 1 auto;
	min-width: 0;
	display: flex;
	flex-direction: column;
	gap: 1px;
}

/* flex: 0 0 auto so this row doesn't stretch vertically inside text-col's
   column stacking -- the title inside it still shrinks/ellipsizes normally,
   since that's a separate (horizontal) axis concern. */
.working-tabs-title-row {
	display: flex;
	flex: 0 0 auto;
	align-items: baseline;
	gap: 6px;
	min-width: 0;
}

.working-tabs-description {
	font-size: 11px;
	color: var(--text-faint);
	white-space: nowrap;
	overflow: hidden;
	text-overflow: ellipsis;
}

.working-tabs-wrap-titles .working-tabs-description {
	white-space: normal;
	overflow: visible;
	text-overflow: clip;
	word-break: break-word;
}

.working-tabs-count {
	flex: 0 0 auto;
	font-size: 11px;
	color: var(--text-faint);
	background-color: var(--background-modifier-border);
	border-radius: 10px;
	padding: 0 6px;
	line-height: 16px;
	min-width: 16px;
	text-align: center;
}

.working-tabs-focus-badge {
	flex: 0 0 auto;
	font-size: 10px;
	color: var(--text-accent);
	text-transform: lowercase;
	letter-spacing: 0.02em;
}

.working-tabs-section-header.is-focused-section .working-tabs-title {
	color: var(--interactive-accent, #7c6ff0);
}

/* A live group keeps a normal title. The chip and the fill say it is open;
   recolouring the words made them hard to read on the tint. */
.working-tabs-live-chip {
	flex: 0 0 auto;
	font-size: 10px;
	line-height: 16px;
	padding: 0 6px;
	border-radius: 10px;
	color: var(--text-normal);
	background-color: var(--background-primary);
	border: 1px solid var(--background-modifier-border);
}

/* Neutral bar for every group. Colour fill is only for a group whose pane
   is on screen, so a long hibernating list stays a list of names. The stripe
   on the left still carries that group's colour. */
.working-tabs-group-header {
	background-color: var(--background-modifier-active, var(--background-modifier-hover));
}

.working-tabs-cluster.is-onscreen .working-tabs-group-header.working-tabs-colored {
	background-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--working-tabs-accent) 36%, transparent);
}

.working-tabs-group-header:hover {
	background-color: var(--background-modifier-hover);
}

.working-tabs-cluster.is-onscreen .working-tabs-group-header.working-tabs-colored:hover {
	background-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--working-tabs-accent) 48%, transparent);
}

.working-tabs-screen-state:empty {
	display: none;
}

.working-tabs-screen-state {
	flex: 0 0 auto;
	font-size: 10px;
	letter-spacing: 0.02em;
	text-transform: lowercase;
}

.working-tabs-screen-state[data-state='on'] {
	color: var(--text-accent);
}

.working-tabs-screen-state[data-state='off'] {
	color: var(--text-faint);
}

/* Marks the pane that belongs to the group selected in the sidebar.
   Outline only — it must not change the split's flex sizes. */
.workspace-tabs.working-tabs-selected-pane {
	outline: 2px solid var(--interactive-accent, #7c6ff0);
	outline-offset: -2px;
}

/* Marked "tucked away" -- sidebar-only, doesn't touch the real pane. */
.working-tabs-group-header.is-hidden-pane {
	opacity: 0.55;
}

/* Always in the DOM (for keyboard/touch access) but only visually revealed
   on hover. margin-left: auto pushes it to the row's right edge regardless
   of how short the title+count on the left are. */
.working-tabs-row-actions {
	flex: 0 0 auto;
	display: flex;
	gap: 6px;
	margin-left: auto;
	opacity: 0;
}

.working-tabs-row:hover .working-tabs-row-actions,
.working-tabs-row:focus-within .working-tabs-row-actions {
	opacity: 1;
}

.working-tabs-action-btn {
	width: 22px;
	height: 22px;
	border-radius: 5px;
	display: inline-flex;
	align-items: center;
	justify-content: center;
	color: var(--text-muted);
	cursor: pointer;
}

.working-tabs-action-btn svg {
	width: 16px;
	height: 16px;
}

.working-tabs-action-btn:hover {
	color: var(--text-normal);
	background-color: var(--background-modifier-border);
}

.working-tabs-done-checkbox {
	flex: 0 0 auto;
	margin: 2px 0 0;
	cursor: pointer;
}

.working-tabs-rename-input {
	flex: 1 1 auto;
	min-width: 0;
	font-size: 13px;
	font-weight: 500;
	color: var(--text-normal);
	background-color: var(--background-primary);
	border: 1px solid var(--interactive-accent, #7c6ff0);
	border-radius: 4px;
	padding: 1px 4px;
}

/* Separates everything live (above) from the Completed archive (below),
   Workona-style. The top edge of the panel needs no divider of its own --
   the search input's border-bottom already marks it. */
.working-tabs-divider {
	height: 1px;
	background-color: var(--background-modifier-border);
	margin: 6px 4px;
	flex: 0 0 auto;
}

.working-tabs-cluster {
	margin: 4px 6px 0;
	padding: 2px 2px 8px;
	border-bottom: 1px solid var(--background-modifier-border);
}

.working-tabs-cluster.is-onscreen {
	background-color: var(--background-modifier-hover);
	border-radius: 8px;
	border-bottom-color: transparent;
	margin-bottom: 8px;
}

.working-tabs-cluster.is-hibernating {
	margin-top: 10px;
}

.working-tabs-cluster.is-sections {
	margin-top: 10px;
	border-bottom: none;
}

.working-tabs-cluster-label {
	display: flex;
	align-items: center;
	gap: 8px;
	padding: 8px 8px 4px;
	color: var(--text-muted);
	font-size: var(--font-ui-smaller);
	font-weight: 600;
	letter-spacing: 0.06em;
	text-transform: uppercase;
}

.working-tabs-cluster-label .working-tabs-count {
	margin-left: auto;
	color: var(--text-faint);
	letter-spacing: 0;
	font-weight: 500;
}

.working-tabs-title-row .working-tabs-count {
	color: var(--text-normal);
	background-color: var(--background-primary);
}

/* The "+ New group" / "+ Create a section" pair, sitting between the groups
   block and the sections block. */
.working-tabs-new-group-row .working-tabs-title,
.working-tabs-create-section-row .working-tabs-title {
	color: var(--text-muted);
	font-weight: 400;
}

.working-tabs-new-group-row:hover .working-tabs-title,
.working-tabs-create-section-row:hover .working-tabs-title {
	color: var(--text-normal);
}

.working-tabs-create-section-row {
	border-top: 1px solid var(--background-modifier-border);
	padding-top: 8px;
	margin-top: 4px;
}

.working-tabs-done-toggle {
	display: flex;
	align-items: center;
	gap: 4px;
	padding: 4px 8px;
	font-size: 11px;
	color: var(--text-faint);
	cursor: pointer;
	border-radius: 6px;
}

.working-tabs-done-toggle:hover {
	background-color: var(--background-modifier-hover);
	color: var(--text-muted);
}

/*
 * "Hide pane" -- ported from Vertical Tabs' own proven approach (same idea,
 * different class name so the two plugins never collide if both installed):
 * hide the specific pane, then let a *declarative* CSS `:has()` selector
 * cascade the collapse up through however many nested splits are affected,
 * rather than us walking the DOM in JavaScript to replicate that (which is
 * what corrupted an unrelated pane's sizing in an earlier attempt here).
 * `:has()` re-evaluates on its own whenever the DOM changes, so there's no
 * JS state (snapshotted flex values, etc.) that can drift out of sync with
 * reality -- the failure mode that caused that corruption.
 */
/* Group colour is a light tint on the tab face. The selected tab is that
   same tint plus one hairline border. The multi-row tab snippet paints every
   active tab solid orange with !important, so these rules have to match that
   weight, and only on panes this plugin has coloured. */
.workspace-tabs.working-tabs-accented {
	box-shadow: inset 3px 0 0 var(--working-tabs-accent);
	--tab-outline-width: 0px;
	--tab-outline-color: transparent;
}

.workspace-split.mod-root .workspace-tabs.working-tabs-accented .workspace-tab-header,
.workspace-split.mod-root .workspace-tabs.working-tabs-accented .workspace-tab-header.is-active,
.workspace-split.mod-root .workspace-tabs.working-tabs-accented .workspace-tab-header.is-active::before,
.workspace-split.mod-root .workspace-tabs.working-tabs-accented .workspace-tab-header.is-active::after {
	background: transparent !important;
	background-color: transparent !important;
	background-image: none !important;
	box-shadow: none !important;
	outline: none !important;
	border: none !important;
	border-bottom: none !important;
	font-weight: 400 !important;
	color: var(--text-normal) !important;
}

.workspace-split.mod-root .workspace-tabs.working-tabs-accented .workspace-tab-header .workspace-tab-header-inner {
	background-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--working-tabs-accent) 22%, var(--background-primary)) !important;
	border: 1px solid transparent !important;
	border-radius: var(--tab-radius, var(--radius-s, 6px));
	box-shadow: none !important;
	color: var(--text-normal) !important;
	font-weight: 400 !important;
}

.workspace-split.mod-root .workspace-tabs.working-tabs-accented .workspace-tab-header.is-active .workspace-tab-header-inner {
	border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--text-normal) 75%, transparent) !important;
}

.workspace-split.mod-root .workspace-tabs.working-tabs-accented .workspace-tab-header-inner-title,
.workspace-split.mod-root .workspace-tabs.working-tabs-accented .workspace-tab-header-inner-icon {
	color: var(--text-normal) !important;
	font-weight: 400 !important;
}

.modal.mod-working-tabs-editor {
	width: 92vw !important;
	max-width: 92vw !important;
	height: 86vh !important;
	max-height: 86vh !important;
	display: flex;
	flex-direction: column;
	padding: 12px;

}

.modal.mod-working-tabs-editor .modal-content.working-tabs-editor-modal {
	flex: 1 1 auto;
	min-height: 0;
	height: 100%;
	max-height: none;

	overflow: hidden;

	padding: 0;

}

.modal.mod-working-tabs-editor .working-tabs-editor-host {
	display: flex;
	flex: 1 1 auto;
	min-height: 0;
	width: 100%;
	height: 100%;
	background-color: var(--background-primary);
}

.modal.mod-working-tabs-editor .working-tabs-editor-leaf,
.modal.mod-working-tabs-editor .working-tabs-editor-leaf .workspace-leaf-content,
.modal.mod-working-tabs-editor .working-tabs-editor-leaf .view-content,
.modal.mod-working-tabs-editor .working-tabs-editor-leaf .markdown-source-view,
.modal.mod-working-tabs-editor .working-tabs-editor-leaf .cm-editor,
.modal.mod-working-tabs-editor .working-tabs-editor-leaf .cm-scroller {
	width: 100%;

}

.working-tabs-tab-row.working-tabs-colored {
	background-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--working-tabs-accent) 16%, transparent);
}

.working-tabs-tab-row.working-tabs-colored:hover {
	background-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--working-tabs-accent) 28%, var(--background-modifier-hover));
}

/* The colour circle beside each name in the colour menu -- see colorMenuTitle
   in TabSpacesView. Centred rather than sat on the baseline (a circle has no
   descender to line up), and ringed so the pale end of the palette -- yellow
   especially -- still reads against a light theme's menu background. */
.working-tabs-swatch {
	display: inline-block;
	width: 11px;
	height: 11px;
	margin-right: 9px;
	border-radius: 50%;
	vertical-align: middle;
	background-color: var(--working-tabs-accent);
	box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--background-modifier-border);
}

/* Drag affordance and drop indicators */

.working-tabs-dragging {
	opacity: 0.5;
}

.working-tabs-drop-before::before,
.working-tabs-drop-after::after {
	content: '';
	position: absolute;
	left: 8px;
	right: 8px;
	height: 2px;
	border-radius: 1px;
	background-color: var(--interactive-accent, #7c6ff0);
}

.working-tabs-drop-before::before {
	top: 0;
}

.working-tabs-drop-after::after {
	bottom: 0;
}

.working-tabs-drop-into {
	background-color: var(--background-modifier-border);
	outline: 1px solid var(--interactive-accent, #7c6ff0);
	outline-offset: -1px;
}

.working-tabs-pool {
	margin: 2px 8px 6px;
	border: 1px dashed var(--background-modifier-border);
	background-color: transparent;
}

.working-tabs-pool.is-drop {
	border-color: var(--interactive-accent);

}

.working-tabs-pool-label {
	padding: 4px 8px 0;
	color: var(--text-muted);
	font-size: var(--font-ui-smaller);
	letter-spacing: 0.04em;
	text-transform: uppercase;
}

.working-tabs-pool-empty {
	padding: 2px 8px 6px;
	color: var(--text-faint);
}

.working-tabs-origin {
	margin-left: 8px;
	color: var(--text-faint);
	font-size: var(--font-ui-smaller);
}

.working-tabs-row.is-picked {
	box-shadow: inset 2px 0 0 var(--interactive-accent);
}

.workspace-leaf.working-tabs-viewport-drop.is-center {
	box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--interactive-accent);
}

.workspace-leaf.working-tabs-viewport-drop.is-left {
	box-shadow: inset 8px 0 0 var(--interactive-accent);
}

.workspace-leaf.working-tabs-viewport-drop.is-right {
	box-shadow: inset -8px 0 0 var(--interactive-accent);
}

.workspace-leaf.working-tabs-viewport-drop.is-top {
	box-shadow: inset 0 8px 0 var(--interactive-accent);
}

.workspace-leaf.working-tabs-viewport-drop.is-bottom {
	box-shadow: inset 0 -8px 0 var(--interactive-accent);
}

/* "Hide tab bar" setting -- scoped to `.mod-root` (Obsidian's own class for
   the main/center split, as opposed to `.mod-left-split`/`.mod-right-split`
   for the sidebar docks) so it only ever touches note-tab headers in the
   first place. Hiding broadly and then trying to restore the sidebar's own
   pane-switcher row (same element class, different use) shifted its
   position by a couple pixels -- scoping up front avoids touching the
   sidebar's DOM at all, not just hiding it differently. */
body.working-tabs-hide-tab-headers .mod-root .workspace-tab-header-container {
	display: none;
}

/* Colour-coding palette. Declared on `body` (not :root) because that's where
   Obsidian declares the --color-* variables these defer to -- a var() reference
   only resolves against the element the property is declared on, so hoisting
   these to :root would silently leave every one of them invalid. Deferring to
   Obsidian's own colours rather than fixed hexes is what makes a group keep
   looking right across a theme switch; the fallbacks only come into play if a
   theme drops one. See COLOR_SLOTS in types.ts -- the two lists must match. */
body {
	--working-tabs-color-blue: var(--color-blue, #4a7fe0);
	--working-tabs-color-purple: var(--color-purple, #8b6fd6);
	--working-tabs-color-green: var(--color-green, #43a047);
	--working-tabs-color-orange: var(--color-orange, #e08b3c);
	--working-tabs-color-cyan: var(--color-cyan, #2fa3a3);
	--working-tabs-color-pink: var(--color-pink, #d45d97);
	--working-tabs-color-yellow: var(--color-yellow, #d0a215);
	--working-tabs-color-red: var(--color-red, #d1453b);
}

.working-tabs-text-col {

/* "Hide tab bar" setting -- scoped to `.mod-root` (Obsidian's own class for

   sidebar's DOM at all, not just hiding it differently. */
body.working-tabs-hide-tab-headers .mod-root .workspace-tab-header-container {

}

/* Colour-coding palette. Declared on `body` (not :root) because that's where
   Obsidian declares the --color-* variables these defer to -- a var() reference
   only resolves against the element the property is declared on, so hoisting
   these to :root would silently leave every one of them invalid. Deferring to
   Obsidian's own colours rather than fixed hexes is what makes a group keep
   looking right across a theme switch; the fallbacks only come into play if a
   theme drops one. See COLOR_SLOTS in types.ts -- the two lists must match. */
body {
	--working-tabs-color-blue: var(--color-blue, #4a7fe0);
	--working-tabs-color-purple: var(--color-purple, #8b6fd6);
	--working-tabs-color-green: var(--color-green, #43a047);
	--working-tabs-color-orange: var(--color-orange, #e08b3c);
	--working-tabs-color-cyan: var(--color-cyan, #2fa3a3);
	--working-tabs-color-pink: var(--color-pink, #d45d97);
	--working-tabs-color-yellow: var(--color-yellow, #d0a215);
	--working-tabs-color-red: var(--color-red, #d1453b);
}

.working-tabs-view {
	display: flex;
	flex-direction: column;
	height: 100%;
}

	display: inline-flex;
	align-items: center;

.working-tabs-row.working-tabs-colored::before {

.working-tabs-cluster.is-sections .working-tabs-group-header:hover,
.working-tabs-cluster.is-sections .working-tabs-group-header.working-tabs-colored:hover,

.working-tabs-cluster.is-sections .working-tabs-tab-row.working-tabs-colored,

.working-tabs-cluster.is-sections .working-tabs-section-header {

}

.working-tabs-text-col {
	flex: 1 1 auto;
	min-width: 0;
	display: flex;
	flex-direction: column;
	gap: 1px;
}

/* flex: 0 0 auto so this row doesn't stretch vertically inside text-col's
   column stacking -- the title inside it still shrinks/ellipsizes normally,
   since that's a separate (horizontal) axis concern. */
.working-tabs-title-row {
	display: flex;
	flex: 0 0 auto;
	align-items: baseline;
	gap: 6px;
	min-width: 0;
}

.working-tabs-description {
	font-size: 11px;
	color: var(--text-faint);
	white-space: nowrap;
	overflow: hidden;
	text-overflow: ellipsis;
}

.working-tabs-wrap-titles .working-tabs-description {
	white-space: normal;
	overflow: visible;
	text-overflow: clip;
	word-break: break-word;
}

.working-tabs-count {
	flex: 0 0 auto;
	font-size: 11px;
	color: var(--text-faint);
	background-color: var(--background-modifier-border);
	border-radius: 10px;
	padding: 0 6px;
	line-height: 16px;
	min-width: 16px;
	text-align: center;
}

.working-tabs-focus-badge {
	flex: 0 0 auto;
	font-size: 10px;
	color: var(--text-accent);
	text-transform: lowercase;
	letter-spacing: 0.02em;
}

.working-tabs-section-header.is-focused-section .working-tabs-title {
	color: var(--interactive-accent, #7c6ff0);
}

/* A live group keeps a normal title. The chip and the fill say it is open;
   recolouring the words made them hard to read on the tint. */
.working-tabs-live-chip {
	flex: 0 0 auto;
	font-size: 10px;
	line-height: 16px;
	padding: 0 6px;
	border-radius: 10px;
	color: var(--text-normal);
	background-color: var(--background-primary);
	border: 1px solid var(--background-modifier-border);
}

/* Neutral bar for every group. Colour fill is only for a group whose pane
   is on screen, so a long hibernating list stays a list of names. The stripe
   on the left still carries that group's colour. */
.working-tabs-group-header {
	background-color: var(--background-modifier-active, var(--background-modifier-hover));
}

.working-tabs-cluster.is-onscreen .working-tabs-group-header.working-tabs-colored {
	background-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--working-tabs-accent) 36%, transparent);
}

.working-tabs-group-header:hover {
	background-color: var(--background-modifier-hover);
}

.working-tabs-cluster.is-onscreen .working-tabs-group-header.working-tabs-colored:hover {
	background-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--working-tabs-accent) 48%, transparent);
}

.working-tabs-screen-state:empty {
	display: none;
}

.working-tabs-screen-state {
	flex: 0 0 auto;
	font-size: 10px;
	letter-spacing: 0.02em;
	text-transform: lowercase;
}

.working-tabs-screen-state[data-state='on'] {
	color: var(--text-accent);
}

.working-tabs-screen-state[data-state='off'] {
	color: var(--text-faint);
}

/* Marks the pane that belongs to the group selected in the sidebar.
   Outline only — it must not change the split's flex sizes. */
.workspace-tabs.working-tabs-selected-pane {
	outline: 2px solid var(--interactive-accent, #7c6ff0);
	outline-offset: -2px;
}

/* Marked "tucked away" -- sidebar-only, doesn't touch the real pane. */
.working-tabs-group-header.is-hidden-pane {
	opacity: 0.55;
}

/* Always in the DOM (for keyboard/touch access) but only visually revealed
   on hover. margin-left: auto pushes it to the row's right edge regardless
   of how short the title+count on the left are. */
.working-tabs-row-actions {
	flex: 0 0 auto;
	display: flex;
	gap: 6px;
	margin-left: auto;
	opacity: 0;
}

.working-tabs-row:hover .working-tabs-row-actions,
.working-tabs-row:focus-within .working-tabs-row-actions {
	opacity: 1;
}

.working-tabs-action-btn {
	width: 22px;
	height: 22px;
	border-radius: 5px;
	display: inline-flex;
	align-items: center;
	justify-content: center;
	color: var(--text-muted);
	cursor: pointer;
}

.working-tabs-action-btn svg {
	width: 16px;
	height: 16px;
}

.working-tabs-action-btn:hover {
	color: var(--text-normal);
	background-color: var(--background-modifier-border);
}

.working-tabs-done-checkbox {
	flex: 0 0 auto;
	margin: 2px 0 0;
	cursor: pointer;
}

.working-tabs-rename-input {
	flex: 1 1 auto;
	min-width: 0;
	font-size: 13px;
	font-weight: 500;
	color: var(--text-normal);
	background-color: var(--background-primary);
	border: 1px solid var(--interactive-accent, #7c6ff0);
	border-radius: 4px;
	padding: 1px 4px;
}

/* Separates everything live (above) from the Completed archive (below),
   Workona-style. The top edge of the panel needs no divider of its own --
   the search input's border-bottom already marks it. */
.working-tabs-divider {
	height: 1px;
	background-color: var(--background-modifier-border);
	margin: 6px 4px;
	flex: 0 0 auto;
}

.working-tabs-cluster {
	margin: 4px 6px 0;
	padding: 2px 2px 8px;
	border-bottom: 1px solid var(--background-modifier-border);
}

.working-tabs-cluster.is-onscreen {
	background-color: var(--background-modifier-hover);
	border-radius: 8px;
	border-bottom-color: transparent;
	margin-bottom: 8px;
}

.working-tabs-cluster.is-hibernating {
	margin-top: 10px;
}

.working-tabs-cluster.is-sections {
	margin-top: 10px;
	border-bottom: none;
}

.working-tabs-cluster-label {
	display: flex;
	align-items: center;
	gap: 8px;
	padding: 8px 8px 4px;
	color: var(--text-muted);
	font-size: var(--font-ui-smaller);
	font-weight: 600;
	letter-spacing: 0.06em;
	text-transform: uppercase;
}

.working-tabs-cluster-label .working-tabs-count {
	margin-left: auto;
	color: var(--text-faint);
	letter-spacing: 0;
	font-weight: 500;
}

.working-tabs-title-row .working-tabs-count {
	color: var(--text-normal);

}

/* The "+ New group" / "+ Create a section" pair, sitting between the groups
   block and the sections block. */
.working-tabs-new-group-row .working-tabs-title,
.working-tabs-create-section-row .working-tabs-title {
	color: var(--text-muted);
	font-weight: 400;
}

.working-tabs-new-group-row:hover .working-tabs-title,
.working-tabs-create-section-row:hover .working-tabs-title {
	color: var(--text-normal);
}

.working-tabs-create-section-row {
	border-top: 1px solid var(--background-modifier-border);
	padding-top: 8px;
	margin-top: 4px;
}

.working-tabs-done-toggle {
	display: flex;
	align-items: center;
	gap: 4px;
	padding: 4px 8px;
	font-size: 11px;
	color: var(--text-faint);
	cursor: pointer;
	border-radius: 6px;
}

.working-tabs-done-toggle:hover {
	background-color: var(--background-modifier-hover);
	color: var(--text-muted);
}

/*
 * "Hide pane" -- ported from Vertical Tabs' own proven approach (same idea,
 * different class name so the two plugins never collide if both installed):
 * hide the specific pane, then let a *declarative* CSS `:has()` selector
 * cascade the collapse up through however many nested splits are affected,
 * rather than us walking the DOM in JavaScript to replicate that (which is
 * what corrupted an unrelated pane's sizing in an earlier attempt here).
 * `:has()` re-evaluates on its own whenever the DOM changes, so there's no
 * JS state (snapshotted flex values, etc.) that can drift out of sync with
 * reality -- the failure mode that caused that corruption.
 */
/* Group colour is a light tint on the tab face. The selected tab is that
   same tint plus one hairline border. The multi-row tab snippet paints every
   active tab solid orange with !important, so these rules have to match that
   weight, and only on panes this plugin has coloured. */
.workspace-tabs.working-tabs-accented {
	box-shadow: inset 3px 0 0 var(--working-tabs-accent);
	--tab-outline-width: 0px;
	--tab-outline-color: transparent;
}

.workspace-split.mod-root .workspace-tabs.working-tabs-accented .workspace-tab-header,
.workspace-split.mod-root .workspace-tabs.working-tabs-accented .workspace-tab-header.is-active,
.workspace-split.mod-root .workspace-tabs.working-tabs-accented .workspace-tab-header.is-active::before,
.workspace-split.mod-root .workspace-tabs.working-tabs-accented .workspace-tab-header.is-active::after {
	background: transparent !important;
	background-color: transparent !important;
	background-image: none !important;
	box-shadow: none !important;
	outline: none !important;
	border: none !important;
	border-bottom: none !important;
	font-weight: 400 !important;
	color: var(--text-normal) !important;
}

.workspace-split.mod-root .workspace-tabs.working-tabs-accented .workspace-tab-header .workspace-tab-header-inner {
	background-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--working-tabs-accent) 22%, var(--background-primary)) !important;
	background-image: none !important;
	border: 1px solid transparent !important;
	border-radius: var(--tab-radius, var(--radius-s, 6px));
	box-shadow: none !important;
	outline: none !important;
	color: var(--text-normal) !important;
	font-weight: 400 !important;
}

.workspace-split.mod-root .workspace-tabs.working-tabs-accented .workspace-tab-header.is-active .workspace-tab-header-inner {
	border-color: var(--tab-background-selected, var(--interactive-accent, #b35209)) !important;
}

.workspace-split.mod-root .workspace-tabs.working-tabs-accented .workspace-tab-header-inner-title,
.workspace-split.mod-root .workspace-tabs.working-tabs-accented .workspace-tab-header-inner-icon {
	color: var(--text-normal) !important;
	font-weight: 400 !important;
}

/* The colour circle beside each name in the colour menu -- see colorMenuTitle
   in TabSpacesView. Centred rather than sat on the baseline (a circle has no
   descender to line up), and ringed so the pale end of the palette -- yellow
   especially -- still reads against a light theme's menu background. */
.working-tabs-swatch {
	display: inline-block;

	height: 11px;

.working-tabs-pool-label {

.working-tabs-pool-empty {

.working-tabs-origin {

	color: var(--text-faint);

.working-tabs-row.is-picked {

}

.workspace-leaf.working-tabs-viewport-drop.is-top {

}

.workspace-leaf.working-tabs-viewport-drop.is-bottom {

}

/* "Hide tab bar" setting -- scoped to `.mod-root` (Obsidian's own class for
   the main/center split, as opposed to `.mod-left-split`/`.mod-right-split`
   for the sidebar docks) so it only ever touches note-tab headers in the
   first place. Hiding broadly and then trying to restore the sidebar's own
   pane-switcher row (same element class, different use) shifted its
   position by a couple pixels -- scoping up front avoids touching the
   sidebar's DOM at all, not just hiding it differently. */
body.working-tabs-hide-tab-headers .mod-root .workspace-tab-header-container {
	display: none;
}

```
import type { SpaceNode } from './types';
import { COMPLETED_PARENT_ID } from './types';

/** Minimal view-state shape used by blank-tab detection -- avoids importing Obsidian. */
export type PlanViewState = { type?: string; state?: Record<string, unknown> };

export interface TabIdentity {
	key: string;
	path?: string;
	title: string;
}

export interface SnapshotLeaf {
	leafId: string;
	identity: TabIdentity;
	viewState?: PlanViewState;
}

export interface SnapshotPane {
	paneId: string;
	leaves: SnapshotLeaf[];
}

export interface WorkspaceSnapshot {
	panes: SnapshotPane[];
}

export interface PlanContext {
	mode: 'full' | 'poll';
	focusedSectionId: string | null;
	suppressedGroupIds: ReadonlySet<string>;
	nextDefaultTitle: () => string;
}

export type PlanEntry =
	| { kind: 'claimPane'; groupId: string; paneId: string }
	| { kind: 'releasePane'; groupId: string }
	| { kind: 'syncTitle'; tabId: string; title: string }
	| { kind: 'syncViewState'; tabId: string; viewState: PlanViewState }
	| { kind: 'setOrder'; tabId: string; order: number }
	| { kind: 'moveTabRecord'; tabId: string; fromGroupId: string; toGroupId: string }
	| { kind: 'addTab'; groupId: string; key: string; path?: string; title: string; viewState?: PlanViewState }
	| { kind: 'pruneTab'; tabId: string }
	| { kind: 'newGroup'; paneId: string; parentId: string | null; title: string }
	| { kind: 'merged'; fromGroup: SpaceNode; toGroupId: string; tabIds: string[] }
	| { kind: 'removeGroup'; groupId: string };

/** Provisional groupId on addTab entries that follow a newGroup for the same pane. */
export function pendingGroupId(paneId: string): string {
	return `__new__:${paneId}`;
}

/** A tab with nothing to restore -- a blank "New tab" pane. */
export function isBlankTab(tab: SpaceNode): boolean {
	if (tab.filePath) return false;
	const type = (tab.viewState as PlanViewState | undefined)?.type;
	return !type || type === 'empty';
}

/** Stored hide flags only. Focus does not hide panes — that pulled flex items out of Obsidian's split tree. */
export function effectivelyHidden(
	group: Pick<SpaceNode, 'hidden'>,
	section: Pick<SpaceNode, 'hidden'> | undefined
): boolean {
	if (group.hidden) return true;
	if (section?.hidden) return true;
	return false;
}

function isSessionKey(key: string): boolean {
	return key.includes(':') && !key.includes('/');
}

function isAutoGroupTitle(title: string): boolean {
	return /^Group \d+$/.test(title);
}

function tabKeysOf(nodes: SpaceNode[], groupId: string): Set<string> {
	return new Set(
		childrenOf(nodes, groupId)
			.filter((tab) => !tab.done && tab.tabKey)
			.map((tab) => tab.tabKey as string)
	);
}

/** Best dormant group whose stored files cover this pane. Session-only leaves do not block a match. */
function bestClaim(
	nodes: SpaceNode[],
	paneKeys: string[],
	candidates: SpaceNode[],
	taken: Map<string, string>
): { id: string; overlap: number } | undefined {
	let best: { id: string; overlap: number } | undefined;
	for (const group of candidates) {
		if (taken.has(group.id)) continue;
		const keys = tabKeysOf(nodes, group.id);
		if (keys.size === 0) continue;
		const fileKeys = paneKeys.filter((key) => !isSessionKey(key));
		if (fileKeys.some((key) => !keys.has(key))) continue;
		const overlap = paneKeys.filter((key) => keys.has(key)).length;
		if (overlap === 0) continue;
		if (!best || overlap > best.overlap) best = { id: group.id, overlap };
	}
	return best;
}

/** A tab filed in a section pool. Its leaf may still be open; the record stays put. */
function isSectionPool(nodes: SpaceNode[], tab: SpaceNode): boolean {
	if (tab.type !== 'tab' || !tab.parentId) return false;
	return nodes.some((node) => node.id === tab.parentId && node.type === 'section');
}

function childrenOf(nodes: SpaceNode[], parentId: string): SpaceNode[] {
	return nodes
		.filter((n) => n.parentId === parentId)
		.sort((a, b) => a.order - b.order);
}

/**
 * Pure membership plan: workspace snapshot + store nodes → ordered PlanEntry list.
 * No Obsidian imports; LeafSync applies the result inside one store.batch.
 */
export function plan(
	snapshot: WorkspaceSnapshot,
	nodes: SpaceNode[],
	ctx: PlanContext
): PlanEntry[] {
	const entries: PlanEntry[] = [];
	const paneById = new Map(snapshot.panes.map((p) => [p.paneId, p]));
	const paneIds = new Set(paneById.keys());

	const tabs = nodes.filter((n) => n.type === 'tab');
	const tabByKey = new Map<string, SpaceNode>();
	for (const tab of tabs) {
		if (tab.tabKey) tabByKey.set(tab.tabKey, tab);
	}

	const groups = nodes.filter((n) => n.type === 'group' && n.parentId !== COMPLETED_PARENT_ID);

	// Effective parent of each tab after moves emitted this pass (pure — no node mutation).
	const effectiveParent = new Map<string, string>();
	for (const tab of tabs) {
		if (tab.parentId) effectiveParent.set(tab.id, tab.parentId);
	}

	const claimByGroup = new Map<string, string>();
	const claimByPane = new Map<string, string>();
	for (const g of groups) {
		if (g.homePaneId && paneIds.has(g.homePaneId)) {
			claimByGroup.set(g.id, g.homePaneId);
			claimByPane.set(g.homePaneId, g.id);
		}
	}

	const addedThisPass = new Set<string>();
	const hasKey = (groupId: string, key: string): boolean => {
		if (addedThisPass.has(`${groupId}\0${key}`)) return true;
		return childrenOf(nodes, groupId).some((tab) => tab.type === 'tab' && tab.tabKey === key);
	};
	const rememberKey = (groupId: string, key: string): void => {
		addedThisPass.add(`${groupId}\0${key}`);
	};
	const movedOut = new Map<string, { toGroupId: string; tabIds: string[] }>();
	const movedTabIds = new Set<string>();

	// 1. Live sync
	for (const pane of snapshot.panes) {
		for (const leaf of pane.leaves) {
			const tab = tabByKey.get(leaf.identity.key);
			if (!tab) continue;
			if (!tab.titleOverridden && tab.title !== leaf.identity.title) {
				entries.push({ kind: 'syncTitle', tabId: tab.id, title: leaf.identity.title });
			}
			if (ctx.mode === 'full' && leaf.viewState) {
				entries.push({ kind: 'syncViewState', tabId: tab.id, viewState: leaf.viewState });
			}
		}
	}

	// 2. Claims — keep / release
	for (const g of groups) {
		if (!g.homePaneId) continue;
		if (paneIds.has(g.homePaneId)) {
			entries.push({ kind: 'claimPane', groupId: g.id, paneId: g.homePaneId });
		} else {
			entries.push({ kind: 'releasePane', groupId: g.id });
			claimByGroup.delete(g.id);

			let survivors = 0;
			for (const tab of childrenOf(nodes, g.id)) {
				if (!tab.done && isBlankTab(tab)) {
					entries.push({ kind: 'pruneTab', tabId: tab.id });
				} else {
					survivors++;
				}
			}
			if (survivors === 0) {
				entries.push({ kind: 'removeGroup', groupId: g.id });
			}
		}
	}

	// 3. Reattach. After a restart the pane id is gone and some of the group's
	// tabs may not have been restored yet. Claim the pane when every file in it
	// already belongs to one dormant group. A new session-only leaf (terminal
	// leaf ids change every launch) does not block that. Do not prune the
	// group's other stored tabs on this pass.
	const reattachCandidates = groups.filter(
		(g) => !claimByGroup.has(g.id) && g.parentId !== COMPLETED_PARENT_ID
	);
	const freshClaims = new Set<string>();

	for (const pane of snapshot.panes) {
		if (claimByPane.has(pane.paneId)) continue;
		const best = bestClaim(
			nodes,
			pane.leaves.map((leaf) => leaf.identity.key),
			reattachCandidates,
			claimByGroup
		);
		if (!best) continue;
		entries.push({ kind: 'claimPane', groupId: best.id, paneId: pane.paneId });
		claimByGroup.set(best.id, pane.paneId);
		claimByPane.set(pane.paneId, best.id);
		freshClaims.add(best.id);
	}

	// A pane already claimed by an automatic "Group N" goes back to the named
	// group that actually owns those files. Those automatic groups are what a
	// failed reattach left behind.
	for (const [paneId, groupId] of [...claimByPane.entries()]) {
		const owner = groups.find((group) => group.id === groupId);
		if (!owner || !isAutoGroupTitle(owner.title)) continue;
		const pane = paneById.get(paneId);
		if (!pane) continue;
		const paneKeys = pane.leaves.map((leaf) => leaf.identity.key);
		const better = bestClaim(
			nodes,
			paneKeys,
			groups.filter((group) => group.id !== groupId && !isAutoGroupTitle(group.title)),
			claimByGroup
		);
		if (!better) continue;
		const ownerKeys = tabKeysOf(nodes, owner.id);
		const ownerOverlap = paneKeys.filter((key) => ownerKeys.has(key)).length;
		if (better.overlap < ownerOverlap) continue;
		entries.push({ kind: 'releasePane', groupId });
		entries.push({ kind: 'claimPane', groupId: better.id, paneId });
		claimByGroup.delete(groupId);
		claimByGroup.set(better.id, paneId);
		claimByPane.set(paneId, better.id);
		freshClaims.add(better.id);
	}

	// A live group whose pane is gone, and whose non-done tabs all sit in one
	// remaining claimed pane, moves those records instead of copying them.
	// The snapshot has no empty pane, so the later merge step never sees this.
	for (const g of groups) {
		if (claimByGroup.has(g.id) || !g.homePaneId) continue;
		const nonDone = childrenOf(nodes, g.id).filter((t) => !t.done && t.tabKey);
		if (nonDone.length === 0) continue;
		const hosts = snapshot.panes.filter((pane) => {
			const keys = new Set(pane.leaves.map((l) => l.identity.key));
			return nonDone.every((t) => keys.has(t.tabKey as string));
		});
		if (hosts.length !== 1) continue;
		const hostId = claimByPane.get(hosts[0].paneId);
		if (!hostId || hostId === g.id) continue;
		const tabIds: string[] = [];
		for (const tab of nonDone) {
			entries.push({
				kind: 'moveTabRecord',
				tabId: tab.id,
				fromGroupId: g.id,
				toGroupId: hostId,
			});
			movedTabIds.add(tab.id);
			effectiveParent.set(tab.id, hostId);
			tabIds.push(tab.id);
		}
		entries.push({
			kind: 'merged',
			fromGroup: { ...g },
			toGroupId: hostId,
			tabIds,
		});
		entries.push({ kind: 'removeGroup', groupId: g.id });
	}

	// 4. Mirror (D1) — moves/adds for every claimed pane first, then prunes/order.
	// Two passes so a swap between live panes never prune+adds the same key.
	const mirrorTargets: Array<{ paneId: string; groupId: string }> = [];
	for (const [paneId, groupId] of claimByPane) {
		if (ctx.suppressedGroupIds.has(groupId)) continue;
		mirrorTargets.push({ paneId, groupId });
	}

	for (const { paneId, groupId } of mirrorTargets) {
		const pane = paneById.get(paneId);
		if (!pane) continue;

		for (const leaf of pane.leaves) {
			const key = leaf.identity.key;
			const existing = tabByKey.get(key);
			if (!existing) {
				if (hasKey(groupId, key)) continue;
				rememberKey(groupId, key);
				entries.push({
					kind: 'addTab',
					groupId,
					key,
					path: leaf.identity.path,
					title: leaf.identity.title,
					viewState: leaf.viewState,
				});
				continue;
			}

			if (isSectionPool(nodes, existing)) continue;

			const fromId = effectiveParent.get(existing.id);
			if (fromId === groupId) continue;

			const fromGroup = fromId ? groups.find((n) => n.id === fromId) : undefined;
			const fromIsLive = Boolean(fromGroup && claimByGroup.has(fromGroup.id));

			if (fromIsLive && fromGroup) {
				entries.push({
					kind: 'moveTabRecord',
					tabId: existing.id,
					fromGroupId: fromGroup.id,
					toGroupId: groupId,
				});
				movedTabIds.add(existing.id);
				effectiveParent.set(existing.id, groupId);

				const bucket = movedOut.get(fromGroup.id) ?? { toGroupId: groupId, tabIds: [] };
				if (bucket.tabIds.length > 0 && bucket.toGroupId !== groupId) {
					bucket.toGroupId = '';
				} else {
					bucket.toGroupId = groupId;
				}
				bucket.tabIds.push(existing.id);
				movedOut.set(fromGroup.id, bucket);
			} else {
				// Dormant (or unknown) source — leave that list alone; add here
				// unless this group already has the same tab.
				if (hasKey(groupId, key)) continue;
				rememberKey(groupId, key);
				entries.push({
					kind: 'addTab',
					groupId,
					key,
					path: leaf.identity.path,
					title: leaf.identity.title,
					viewState: leaf.viewState,
				});
			}
		}
	}

	for (const { paneId, groupId } of mirrorTargets) {
		const pane = paneById.get(paneId);
		if (!pane) continue;
		const paneKeys = pane.leaves.map((l) => l.identity.key);
		const paneKeySet = new Set(paneKeys);

		for (const tab of childrenOf(nodes, groupId)) {
			if (freshClaims.has(groupId)) continue;
			if (tab.done) continue;
			if (effectiveParent.get(tab.id) !== groupId) continue;
			if (movedTabIds.has(tab.id)) continue;
			if (tab.tabKey && paneKeySet.has(tab.tabKey)) continue;
			// A note that is not open yet still belongs to the group. Dropping it
			// here is what erased stored tabs when a hibernated group was given a pane.
			if (!isBlankTab(tab)) continue;
			entries.push({ kind: 'pruneTab', tabId: tab.id });
		}

		const liveTabs: SpaceNode[] = [];
		const seen = new Set<string>();
		for (const key of paneKeys) {
			const tab = tabByKey.get(key);
			if (!tab || seen.has(tab.id)) continue;
			if (effectiveParent.get(tab.id) !== groupId) continue;
			liveTabs.push(tab);
			seen.add(tab.id);
		}
		const rest = childrenOf(nodes, groupId).filter(
			(t) => effectiveParent.get(t.id) === groupId && !seen.has(t.id)
		);
		let order = 0;
		for (const tab of [...liveTabs, ...rest]) {
			if (tab.order !== order) entries.push({ kind: 'setOrder', tabId: tab.id, order });
			order += 1;
		}
	}

	// 5. Merge detection (D3) — H ends with zero non-done tabs, all moved to a single G
	for (const g of groups) {
		if (!claimByGroup.has(g.id) && !g.homePaneId) continue;
		const move = movedOut.get(g.id);
		if (!move || !move.toGroupId || move.tabIds.length === 0) continue;

		const nonDoneRemaining = tabs.filter(
			(t) => !t.done && effectiveParent.get(t.id) === g.id
		);
		if (nonDoneRemaining.length > 0) continue;

		const paneId = claimByGroup.get(g.id);
		if (paneId) {
			entries.push({ kind: 'releasePane', groupId: g.id });
			claimByGroup.delete(g.id);
			claimByPane.delete(paneId);
		}
		entries.push({
			kind: 'merged',
			fromGroup: { ...g },
			toGroupId: move.toGroupId,
			tabIds: [...move.tabIds],
		});
		entries.push({ kind: 'removeGroup', groupId: g.id });
	}

	// 6. New groups for still-unclaimed panes.
	// A leaf whose record sits in a section pool stays that record. It does not
	// spawn another tab, and a pane of only pooled leaves does not spawn a group.
	for (const pane of snapshot.panes) {
		if (claimByPane.has(pane.paneId)) continue;
		const freshLeaves = pane.leaves.filter((leaf) => {
			const existing = tabByKey.get(leaf.identity.key);
			return !(existing && isSectionPool(nodes, existing));
		});
		if (freshLeaves.length === 0) continue;
		entries.push({
			kind: 'newGroup',
			paneId: pane.paneId,
			parentId: null,
			title: ctx.nextDefaultTitle(),
		});
		const gid = pendingGroupId(pane.paneId);
		const seen = new Set<string>();
		for (const leaf of freshLeaves) {
			if (seen.has(leaf.identity.key)) continue;
			seen.add(leaf.identity.key);
			entries.push({
				kind: 'addTab',
				groupId: gid,
				key: leaf.identity.key,
				path: leaf.identity.path,
				title: leaf.identity.title,
				viewState: leaf.viewState,
			});
		}
		claimByPane.set(pane.paneId, gid);
	}

	// One tab key, one row, inside a single group. Keep the record membership
	// already resolved (tabByKey) and drop the extra copies.
	for (const group of groups) {
		const keeper = new Map<string, string>();
		for (const tab of childrenOf(nodes, group.id)) {
			if (!tab.tabKey) continue;
			const kept = keeper.get(tab.tabKey);
			if (!kept) {
				keeper.set(tab.tabKey, tab.id);
				continue;
			}
			const resolved = tabByKey.get(tab.tabKey)?.id;
			if (resolved === tab.id) {
				entries.push({ kind: 'pruneTab', tabId: kept });
				keeper.set(tab.tabKey, tab.id);
			} else {
				entries.push({ kind: 'pruneTab', tabId: tab.id });
			}
		}
	}

	return entries;
}

import { Notice, TFile, WorkspaceLeaf, type ViewState } from 'obsidian';
import type TabSpacesPlugin from './main';
import type { TabSpacesStore } from './store';
import type { OpenBehavior, SpaceNode } from './types';
import { VIEW_TYPE_WORKING_TABS } from './types';
import {
	effectivelyHidden,
	pendingGroupId,
	plan,
	type PlanEntry,
	type TabIdentity,
	type WorkspaceSnapshot,

import { installPaneMenus } from './pane-menus';
import { needsViewStateForIdentity } from './tab-identity';

/** Every leaf has a runtime `id` (that's what getLeafById() looks up), but it
 * isn't part of the public WorkspaceLeaf type -- this is the standard
 * workaround community plugins use to track a specific pane across renders. */
function getLeafId(leaf: WorkspaceLeaf): string | undefined {
	return (leaf as unknown as { id?: string }).id;
}

/** Session-stable pane ids. `leaf.parent.id` is undocumented and can churn
 * across splits/drags; pinning the first id we see per parent object keeps
 * claims stable for the session (restart still reattaches via membership D7). */
const paneIds = new WeakMap<object, string>();
let paneIdSeq = 0;

export type DockEdge = 'left' | 'right' | 'top' | 'bottom';
type SplitDirectionName = 'vertical' | 'horizontal';

/** The bits of a workspace split or tab group this plugin moves. */
interface SplitNode {
	parent: SplitNode | null;
	children: SplitNode[];
	direction?: 'vertical' | 'horizontal' | null;
	removeChild(child: SplitNode): void;
	insertChild(index: number, child: SplitNode): void;
}

function splitNode(value: unknown): SplitNode {
	return value as SplitNode;
}

function getPaneId(leaf: WorkspaceLeaf): string | undefined {
	const parent = leaf.parent as unknown as { id?: string } | null;
	if (!parent) return undefined;
	const cached = paneIds.get(parent);
	if (cached) return cached;
	const id = parent.id ?? `pane:${++paneIdSeq}`;
	paneIds.set(parent, id);
	return id;
}

/** Derived from the path alone (not leaf.view.getDisplayText()) so it works
 * the same whether or not the leaf's view has actually loaded yet. */
function titleFromPath(path: string): string {
	const base = path.split('/').pop() ?? path;
	return base.replace(/\.[^./]+$/, '') || base;
}

/** How much of a captured `viewState` is worth persisting, per string value.
 * Anything bigger is a payload some view is carrying around, not the identity
 * of a tab we need in order to reopen it -- Terminus, for instance, returns up
 * to 1000 lines of serialized terminal scrollback under `state.scrollback`,
 * which can run to hundreds of KB of escape-code-dense text. Persisting that
 * put a live terminal's whole transcript into this plugin's data.json, made
 * every unrelated store write re-serialize it, and -- because a running
 * terminal's scrollback changes on practically every keystroke -- guaranteed
 * that syncViewState's "has anything changed?" check never once matched, so
 * every reconcile pass wrote the file and re-rendered the sidebar. 8 KB is
 * comfortably above any real identity field (paths, URLs, view modes) and
 * far below any such payload. */
const MAX_VIEW_STATE_VALUE_CHARS = 8 * 1024;

/** How long a poll-driven pass will go without refreshing stored view state.
 * layout-change passes always refresh it, so this only governs the changes no
 * workspace event announces -- chiefly a web viewer tab navigating to a new
 * URL. Half a minute keeps that near-current while keeping the 3s title poll
 * (see start()) off the expensive path. */
const VIEW_STATE_POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 30_000;

/**
 * 'full' passes refresh everything, including each tab's stored view state.
 * 'poll' passes come from the plain interval timer, whose only job is noticing
 * renames no workspace event fires for, and so skip that refresh unless it has
 * been long enough (see VIEW_STATE_POLL_INTERVAL_MS).
 */
type SyncMode = 'full' | 'poll';

/** Strips oversized string values out of a captured view state so only its
 * identity-sized parts get persisted -- e.g. a Terminus tab keeps its `cwd`
 * (which is what makes reopening it land in the right directory) and drops its
 * `scrollback`. Returns the original object untouched when nothing is
 * oversized, which is the case for every ordinary note/canvas/web tab, so the
 * common path allocates nothing. */
function trimViewState(viewState: ViewState): ViewState {
	const state = viewState.state;
	if (!state || typeof state !== 'object') return viewState;
	let oversized: string[] | null = null;
	for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(state)) {
		if (typeof value === 'string' && value.length > MAX_VIEW_STATE_VALUE_CHARS) (oversized ??= []).push(key);
	}
	if (!oversized) return viewState;
	const trimmed = { ...state };
	for (const key of oversized) delete trimmed[key];
	return { ...viewState, state: trimmed };

/**
 * Bridges the plugin's own group/section/tab data (in TabSpacesStore) with
 * Obsidian's live workspace. Nothing here has an analogue in a bookmarks-only
 * plugin, since bookmarks don't track live panes.

export class LeafSync {
	constructor(
		private plugin: TabSpacesPlugin,
		private store: TabSpacesStore

	/** Session-scoped merge undo stack (Phase B); max 5. */
	receipts: Array<{ group: SpaceNode; tabIds: string[]; targetGroupId: string; at: number }> = [];

	private get app() {
		return this.plugin.app;
	}

	private get workspace() {
		return this.plugin.app.workspace;
	}

	 * Identifies a leaf for tracking purposes, whether or not it's backed by a
	 * vault file -- a terminal, an embedded browser tab, a canvas, or any other
	 * plugin's custom view is just as much a "tab" as a note is.
	 *
	 * The file path is read out of the leaf's *stored* view state instead of
	 * `leaf.view instanceof FileView`, because a background pane's view is
	 * often a lightweight `DeferredView` stand-in (not yet instantiated as a
	 * real MarkdownView/FileView) until the user actually clicks into it, so
	 * an instanceof check would silently skip every leaf in any split that
	 * isn't currently focused. The path is also verified against the vault --
	 * some non-file views happen to store an unrelated string under a `file`
	 * key too, which would otherwise get misread as a real path.

	private getTabIdentity(leaf: WorkspaceLeaf): TabIdentity {
		const direct = this.directFilePath(leaf);
		if (direct) return { key: direct, path: direct, title: titleFromPath(direct) };

		const type = leaf.view.getViewType();
		if (!needsViewStateForIdentity(type, direct)) {
			const leafId = getLeafId(leaf) ?? `${Date.now()}-${Math.random()}`;
			return { key: `${type}:${leafId}`, title: leaf.getDisplayText() || type || 'Untitled' };
		}

		const viewState = this.readViewState(leaf);
		const rawFile = viewState.state?.file;
		const path =
			typeof rawFile === 'string' && this.app.vault.getAbstractFileByPath(rawFile) instanceof TFile
				? rawFile
				: undefined;
		if (path) return { key: path, path, title: titleFromPath(path) };

		const leafId = getLeafId(leaf) ?? `${Date.now()}-${Math.random()}`;
		const title = leaf.getDisplayText() || viewState.type || 'Untitled';
		return { key: `${type}:${leafId}`, title };
	}

	/** A loaded file view exposes its path. A deferred view does not. */
	private directFilePath(leaf: WorkspaceLeaf): string | undefined {
		const file = (leaf.view as { file?: { path?: string } }).file;
		if (typeof file?.path !== 'string' || !file.path) return undefined;
		return this.app.vault.getAbstractFileByPath(file.path) instanceof TFile ? file.path : undefined;
	}

	/** The reverse of clicking a tab in the sidebar: given a leaf that just
	 * became active in the workspace, finds the stored tab tracking it (if
	 * any), so the sidebar can highlight/reveal it in turn.

	 * under the group that claims this leaf's pane. */
	findTabForLeaf(leaf: WorkspaceLeaf): SpaceNode | undefined {
		// The open view already knows its file. getViewState() here serialises
		// the whole view (a terminal dumps its scrollback) and forces layout.
		const key = this.openLeafKey(leaf);
		const paneId = getPaneId(leaf);
		const owner = paneId
			? this.store.items.find((item) => item.type === 'group' && item.homePaneId === paneId)
			: undefined;
		if (owner) {
			const inGroup = this.store.children(owner.id).find((item) => item.type === 'tab' && item.tabKey === key);
			if (inGroup) return inGroup;
		}
		return this.store.items.find((item) => item.type === 'tab' && item.tabKey === key);
	}

	/** Identity of a leaf that is already on screen, without reading view state. */
	private openLeafKey(leaf: WorkspaceLeaf): string {
		const file = (leaf.view as { file?: { path?: string } }).file;
		if (typeof file?.path === 'string' && file.path) return file.path;
		const id = getLeafId(leaf);
		const type = leaf.view.getViewType();
		return id ? `${type}:${id}` : this.getTabIdentity(leaf).key;
	}

	private reconcileQueuedMode: SyncMode | null = null;
	private lastViewStateSync = 0;

	 * yet" the same as "closed". */

	/**
	 * Set for the duration of one reconcile pass so each leaf's view state is
	 * read exactly once per pass instead of once per caller.
	 *
	 * `leaf.getViewState()` is not a cheap accessor -- it calls straight
	 * through to the view's own `getState()`, and a view is free to do real
	 * work there (Terminus serializes its entire scrollback buffer). A pass
	 * asked for the same leaf's state two or three times over: once building
	 * its identity, again to sync it, again when adding it to a group. On a
	 * workspace with a couple of live terminals that was several full
	 * serializations every three seconds, on the main thread, which is the
	 * same thread xterm.js needs in order to accept a keystroke.
	 *
	 * Pass-scoped rather than long-lived: view state genuinely does change
	 * between passes, so caching it across them would make the plugin act on
	 * stale data. A WeakMap so a leaf closed mid-pass isn't held alive.
	 */
	private viewStateCache: WeakMap<WorkspaceLeaf, ViewState> | null = null;

	private readViewState(leaf: WorkspaceLeaf): ViewState {
		const cache = this.viewStateCache;
		if (!cache) return leaf.getViewState();
		const cached = cache.get(leaf);
		if (cached) return cached;
		const fresh = leaf.getViewState();
		cache.set(leaf, fresh);
		return fresh;
	}

	start(): void {
		this.workspace.onLayoutReady(() => void this.reconcile());

		// view state here made each of those events serialise terminal scrollback.
		// Titles and membership use the cheap identity. View state waits for the
		// poll interval inside doReconcile.
		this.plugin.registerEvent(this.workspace.on('layout-change', () => void this.reconcile('poll')));

		// A rename made through another plugin's own UI (e.g. Terminus letting
		// you rename a terminal tab) only touches that plugin's internal DOM
		// elements directly -- it doesn't fire any Obsidian workspace event, so

		// so this costs nothing on the (typical) tick where titles are unchanged.
		// Runs in 'poll' mode: titles are all it exists to catch, and the view

		// timer against views that do real work in getState().
		this.plugin.registerInterval(window.setInterval(() => void this.reconcile('poll'), 3000));

		// without this, a renamed file's tab looks "closed" (old path no

		// gets orphaned out of its group instead of renamed in place.
		this.plugin.registerEvent(

	/**
	 * `layout-change` fires often (any tab/pane change), and a reconcile pass
	 * does several sequential awaited store mutations, each of which writes
	 * to disk. Without this guard, a second layout-change firing mid-pass
	 * would start an overlapping reconcile reading/writing the same data
	 * concurrently -- interleaved writes from two passes is exactly what
	 * produced the duplicate/missing tabs seen while testing this. Instead,
	 * a call that arrives while one is already running just requests exactly
	 * one more full pass after the current one finishes.
	 */
	private async reconcile(mode: SyncMode = 'full'): Promise<void> {
		if (this.reconcileRunning) {
			// Never let a cheap poll downgrade a queued full pass -- a real
			// layout change still has to be reconciled in full once the current
			// pass finishes, whatever else arrived in the meantime.
			this.reconcileQueuedMode = this.reconcileQueuedMode === 'full' || mode === 'full' ? 'full' : 'poll';
			return;
		}
		this.reconcileRunning = true;
		try {
			// One disk write and one sidebar re-render for the whole pass,
			// rather than one of each per tab touched (see store.batch).
			this.viewStateCache = new WeakMap();
			await this.store.batch(() => this.doReconcile(mode));
		} finally {
			this.viewStateCache = null;
			this.reconcileRunning = false;
			const queued = this.reconcileQueuedMode;
			if (queued) {
				this.reconcileQueuedMode = null;
				void this.reconcile(queued);
			}
